result: The RL jammer achieves 33% higher attack efficacy and 67% higher stealth than benchmarks, and the proposed detector attains 20% higher detection accuracy than competing detectors against this jammer.
conclusion: The co-evolving adversarial-detection loop provides a stronger benchmark and better detection of zero-day jamming, though the work is confined to classical wireless security rather than quantum information science.

title: Moving-Average Iteration Of Linear Maps
authors: Fabian Wirth Jeremias Epperlein
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider moving-average iteration for fixed complex matrices and place the theory in the general context of Krasnoselskii and Mann iteration. Necessary and sufficient spectral conditions for the asymptotic stability of moving-average iteration are presented in dependence on the fixed window width. For the corresponding region of stability in the complex plane explicit formulas are derived and it is shown that the region is open, convex and semi-algebraic. The regions are shown to be strictly increasing in the window length and the limiting stability region is determined as the window size tends to infinity.
tldr: The paper characterizes the asymptotic stability region of moving-average iterations of fixed complex matrices as a function of the window width, providing explicit, semi-algebraic stability regions that grow monotonically with window length.
motivation: Moving-average iteration is a natural variant of classical Krasnoselskii and Mann iterations used in control and numerical analysis, but its convergence properties for linear maps lacked a complete spectral characterization.
method: The authors embed moving-average iteration into the general framework of Krasnoselskii and Mann iteration, then derive necessary and sufficient spectral conditions for asymptotic stability, computing explicit stability regions in the complex plane as a function of the fixed window width.
result: The stability region is shown to be open, convex, and semi-algebraic, strictly increasing in the window length, and its limiting form as the window size tends to infinity is determined analytically.
conclusion: The work provides a complete spectral theory for moving-average iteration of linear maps, clarifying how window width controls stability and unifying the method within broader iterative-scheme theory.

title: A Global Stochastic Maximum Principle For Forward-backward Stochastic Control Systems With Quadratic Convex Generator And Unbounded Terminal Condition
authors: Ying Hu, Feng Li, Jiaqiang Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a stochastic optimal control problem for forward-backward stochastic control systems with quadratic convex generator and unbounded terminal condition, where the control domain is not necessarily convex. Due to the absence of bounded mean oscillation (BMO) martingales approach, we introduce a new probability measure, under which all subsequent analysis is then carried out under this new measure. Finally, by means of a new approach to the derivation of the adjoint equations, a global stochastic maximum principle is established.
tldr: The paper establishes a global stochastic maximum principle for forward-backward stochastic control systems with quadratic convex generators and unbounded terminal conditions.
motivation: Existing approaches rely on bounded mean oscillation martingales, which fail in this setting, motivating a new probability measure and adjoint equation derivation.
method: The authors introduce a new probability measure under which the analysis is performed, and derive adjoint equations via a novel approach to obtain the maximum principle.
result: A global stochastic maximum principle is proven for non-convex control domains, quadratic convex generators, and unbounded terminal conditions.
conclusion: The work extends stochastic maximum principle theory to a broader class of forward-backward stochastic control problems without BMO assumptions.

title: FrFNO:Injecting The Analytic Mittag-Leffler Propagator Into A Resolution-robust Neural Operator For Space-time Fractional PDEs
authors: Guofei Pang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional partial differential equations couple a memory-dependent time derivative with a nonlocal fractional Laplacian, and their repeated solution under varying fractional orders, initial data, or diffusivity fields is computationally expensive. Neural operators offer a fast surrogate, but standard architectures must relearn the dominant linear fractional evolution from data. We propose the (FrFNO), a resolution-robust conditional operator. It injects the analytic Mittag--Leffler response of the frozen linear part as a once-precomputed, resolution-independent propagator table, and trains a spectral convolutional network only on the residual induced by variable coefficients and nonlinear advection, conditioned continuously on both fractional orders. The central theoretical result is that under zero-shot super-resolution the injected propagator fills the out-of-band modes that a standard Fourier neural operator sets to zero, replacing the out-of-band full-field tail by the smaller residual tail (a [MATH]-independent constant-factor reduction under weak perturbation). The residual and the full solution carry the same Sobolev order, so the advantage is amplitude reduction rather than a steeper tail. Mesh refinement drives the error to a residual-controlled floor. On a nonlinear two-dimensional space--time fractional Burgers problem FrFNO achieves the lowest relative [MATH] error among six baselines (FNO, PINO, PDNO, CNO, DeepONet, U-Net) at the training resolution and under zero-shot super-resolution, yields the smallest spectral phase error, and remains the best at the integer-order limit and for long integration windows. The same construction extends to coupled fractional systems such as fractional Allen-Cahn and Navier--Stokes equations. Code, training scripts, and reference outputs are available at [URL].
tldr: FrFNO injects an analytic Mittag-Leffler propagator into a Fourier neural operator to solve space-time fractional PDEs efficiently and accurately.
motivation: Fractional PDEs are computationally expensive to solve repeatedly across varying orders and parameters, and standard neural operators must learn the dominant linear fractional evolution from scratch.
method: The proposed method precomputes a resolution-independent propagator table from the frozen linear part and trains a spectral convolutional network on the residual conditioned on fractional orders, with a theoretical analysis of zero-shot super-resolution behavior.
result: On a 2D nonlinear space-time fractional Burgers problem, FrFNO achieves the lowest relative error among six baselines at training resolution and under zero-shot super-resolution, with the smallest spectral phase error and robust performance at the integer-order limit and long integration windows.
conclusion: Injecting an analytic propagator improves resolution-robustness and accuracy for fractional PDE surrogates, and the construction extends to coupled fractional systems such as fractional Allen-Cahn and Navier-Stokes equations.

title: Element-wise Convergence Behavior Of Subspace Iteration
authors: Mingyang Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the element-wise convergence behavior of subspace iteration. All results are established for both \(=\) and \(=\). For a diagonal matrix \(\Lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\) with \(|\lambda_1|>\cdots>|\lambda_n|>0\), we analyze the modulus of each entry of the iterative matrix sequence generated by subspace iteration, both without and with the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Under mild assumptions on the initial matrix \(X\in^{n\times m}\), we first derive exact asymptotic expressions for \(|Q_k(i,j)|\) in the subspace iteration without the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure: entries with \(i\neq j\) decay as \((|\lambda_{\max\{i,j\}}|/|\lambda_{\min\{i,j\}}|)^k\), and the deviation of \(|Q_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \(\max\{|\lambda_j|/|\lambda_{j-1}|,|\lambda_{j+1}|/|\lambda_j|\}^{2k}\), with explicit coefficients determined by the LU factorization of \(X\). For the Rayleigh--Ritz variant, we obtain element-wise bounds for the normalized Ritz vectors \(Z_k\). Specifically, for \(|Z_k(i,j)|\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\geq m+1\) decay as \((|\lambda_i|/|\lambda_j|)^k\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\leq m\) decay as \((|\lambda_{m+1}|^2/(|\lambda_i||\lambda_j|))^k\), and the deviation of \(|Z_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \((|\lambda_{m+1}|/|\lambda_j|)^{2k}\). These results give an element-wise description of the convergence behavior of subspace iteration. After an orthogonal or unitary change of basis, the results apply to real symmetric or complex normal matrices.
tldr: This paper derives element-wise asymptotic convergence rates for subspace iteration, both with and without the Rayleigh–Ritz procedure, for diagonal (and after basis change, symmetric/normal) matrices.
motivation: Subspace iteration is a classical algorithm for computing dominant invariant subspaces, but its convergence is typically described only in terms of subspace angles; the authors aim to characterize how individual matrix entries converge.
method: Assuming a diagonal matrix with strictly decreasing modulus eigenvalues, the authors analyze the entry-wise behavior of the iterates Q_k and the Ritz vectors Z_k, using LU factorization of the initial matrix to obtain explicit asymptotic coefficients and decay rates.
result: Off-diagonal entries of Q_k decay as (|λ_max{i,j}|/|λ_min{i,j}|)^k, diagonals converge to 1 at a squared gap rate, and the Rayleigh–Ritz variant yields analogous element-wise bounds for normalized Ritz vectors Z_k; results extend to real symmetric and complex normal matrices via unitary change of basis.
conclusion: The work provides a refined, element-wise picture of subspace iteration convergence that complements standard subspace-angle analyses, with potential use in understanding entry-wise accuracy of eigenvector approximations.

title: Goal-Oriented Communication And Control Co-Design Via Semantic Push-Pull In Industrial IoT
authors: Muhammad Azeem Khan, Yuriy Zacchia Lun, Aamir Mahmood, Piergiuseppe Di Marco, Mikael Gidlund, Fortunato Santucci
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emerging 6G industrial IoT architectures require wireless networked control systems capable of stabilizing diverse control loops over tightly constrained radio resources. Conventional periodic and Age-of-Information (AoI) based scheduling guarantees bounded staleness at the cost of persistent channel saturation. Conversely, pure event-triggered (PureET) strategies minimize transmissions but risk catastrophic silent deterioration when local sensor-side thresholds fail to reflect critical state evolution. To bridge this gap, we propose a communication-control co-design framework governed by a 6G Semantic Layer that independently arbitrates uplink and downlink resources. Instead of relying on freshness, our architecture evaluates the actual control impact of a packet using the state-to-error ratio (SER). We unify this control confidence with channel reliability in terms of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to orchestrate a threshold-based sensor push and a state-aware controller pull mechanism. To ensure equitable resource allocation across dynamically heterogeneous plants, the proposed framework explicitly scales actuation deadbands according to local plant dynamics. Simulations over Rayleigh-faded channels demonstrate that this approach fundamentally shifts the Pareto frontier between transmission rate and control quality. The proposed scheme achieves tracking accuracy comparable to periodic schedulers at a reduced communication overhead, while mitigating the estimation errors characteristic of PureET.
tldr: The paper proposes a 6G semantic communication-control co-design framework using push-pull mechanisms to balance transmission rate and control quality in industrial IoT.
motivation: Conventional periodic and AoI-based scheduling saturate channels, while pure event-triggered schemes risk silent control deterioration, motivating a goal-oriented approach that evaluates actual control impact.
method: It uses a state-to-error ratio (SER) and SNR-based channel reliability to orchestrate threshold-based sensor push and state-aware controller pull, with actuation deadbands scaled by local plant dynamics.
result: Simulations over Rayleigh-faded channels show the scheme shifts the Pareto frontier, achieving tracking accuracy comparable to periodic schedulers with reduced communication overhead and fewer estimation errors than PureET.
conclusion: The proposed semantic push-pull co-design improves industrial IoT control performance under constrained radio resources, bridging the gap between periodic and event-triggered strategies.

title: TPM-Attest: Hardware-Rooted Integrity Attestation As A Kernel-Level Anti-Cheat Alternative For Linux
authors: Anudeep Gedela (GITAM School Of Technology, GITAM University, Visakhapatnam, India), A. Yaswanth
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiplayer PC gaming on Linux faces a structural problem: the anti-cheat systems that publishers require operate as proprietary Ring 0 kernel modules that are architecturally incompatible with Linux's security model, GPL licensing, and stable ABI guarantees. We argue the right response is not to port these invasive modules to Linux, but to replace them entirely. This paper presents TPM-Attest, a hardware-rooted remote attestation framework that uses the Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0 and the Linux Integrity Measurement Architecture (IMA) to prove, cryptographically, that a client booted cleanly and ran only authorised software -- without any kernel driver, without proprietary code, and without scanning player memory. The system intercepts Epic Online Services (EOS) SDK calls via a userspace LD_PRELOAD hook, gates session access on a live TPM quote bound to a server-issued nonce, and constructs an index-prefixed Merkle tree over the IMA log that is immune to duplicate-leaf collision attacks. Across 500 constructed tamper sessions we achieve a 100% detection rate; incremental leaf caching reduces repeat-attestation latency to under 3 seconds on real TPM 2.0 hardware. A controlled red-team evaluation against a live demo game confirms all four file-backed attack vectors are blocked while precisely characterising the two confirmed bypass conditions. The full implementation is released as open-source software.
tldr: TPM-Attest is a hardware-rooted remote attestation framework using TPM 2.0 and Linux IMA to replace invasive kernel-level anti-cheat modules in multiplayer PC gaming.
motivation: Proprietary Ring 0 anti-cheat modules are incompatible with Linux's security model, GPL licensing, and stable ABI guarantees, so the authors argue for replacing rather than porting them.
method: The system uses TPM 2.0 quotes bound to server-issued nonces, intercepts Epic Online Services SDK calls via LD_PRELOAD, and builds an index-prefixed Merkle tree over the IMA log to prevent duplicate-leaf collisions.
result: Across 500 constructed tamper sessions the framework achieved 100% detection, with repeat-attestation latency under 3 seconds on real TPM 2.0 hardware, and red-team evaluation blocked all four file-backed attack vectors while characterizing two bypass conditions.
conclusion: Hardware-rooted attestation can provide a practical kernel-driver-free alternative for anti-cheat on Linux, though residual bypass conditions remain and the approach is open-sourced for further scrutiny.

title: Information Structure Of Defection Decisions In A Colonel Blotto Model Of Deterrence
authors: Tristan Mott, David Grimsman, Keith Paarporn
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In strategic interactions, deterrence is an outcome where one party incentivizes the other party to not participate. This concept can be applied to Colonel Blotto games between two generals where troops can be deterred from following orders by the actions of the opposing general. In this setting, deterrence depends not only on how generals allocate troops, but also on the information available to troops when they decide whether to follow orders or defect. In this work, we study a two-battlefield Colonel Blotto model of deterrence under multiple information structures, ranging from decisions made with only aggregate information to decisions made after local battlefield conditions are observed. We show how different information structures alter the structure of the induced game, affect the existence of equilibria, and substantially change expected utilities. Our findings also prove that the ratio of troops available to each general combined with a capture probability threshold is enough to inform generals about what information they want their troops to have access to.
tldr: The paper studies how different information structures affect troop defection decisions and deterrence outcomes in a two-battlefield Colonel Blotto game.
motivation: Deterrence in strategic interactions depends not only on resource allocation but also on the information available to subordinates when deciding whether to follow orders or defect.
method: The authors analyze a two-battlefield Colonel Blotto model of deterrence under several information structures, ranging from aggregate information to local battlefield observations, and examine the induced game and its equilibria.
result: Different information structures change the game structure, equilibrium existence, and expected utilities; the ratio of available troops and a capture probability threshold determine what information generals prefer their troops to have.
conclusion: Information design is a central strategic element in this classical deterrence model, but the work is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Batched Paillier-Based Hamming-Distance Computation Over Binary Embeddings
authors: Liwen Ouyang Yavor Litchev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Additively homomorphic encryption supports outsourced computation on encrypted binary embeddings, but large-integer arithmetic and data movement can limit throughput. We describe a Paillier-based client that combines a carry-separated binary encoding, table-based encryption, reduced-exponent decryption, CUDA/CGBN arithmetic, persistent device state, and batched retrieval integration. We establish the encoding's correctness and characterize four CPU and GPU client configurations. The lookup configuration uses a 280-bit exponent-size parameter. Across 3 warm-state trials on batches of 10,000 random 512-bit embeddings, the lookup GPU configuration achieved median-batch throughputs of 43,091 encryptions/s and 28,983 Hamming- distance decodes/s. Its amortized costs were 0.0232 ms and 0.0345 ms per vector, corresponding to factors of 453.8 and 200.9 relative to the measured CPU baseline. These implementation- specific results demonstrate the throughput benefits of combining cryptographic precomputation, batched accelerator execution, and persistent runtime state. The study distinguishes warm-batch performance from isolated-request latency and identifies the remaining costs of initialization, transport, and retrieval integration.
tldr: This paper presents a batched, GPU-accelerated Paillier-based client for computing Hamming distances over encrypted binary embeddings, reporting significant throughput gains over a CPU baseline.
motivation: Additively homomorphic encryption enables outsourced computation on encrypted data, but large-integer arithmetic and data movement limit throughput in practice.
method: The authors combine carry-separated binary encoding, table-based encryption, reduced-exponent decryption, CUDA/CGBN arithmetic, persistent device state, and batched retrieval integration, and characterize four CPU and GPU client configurations.
result: On batches of 10,000 random 512-bit embeddings, the lookup GPU configuration achieved median throughputs of 43,091 encryptions/s and 28,983 Hamming-distance decodes/s, with amortized costs of 0.0232 ms and 0.0345 ms per vector, corresponding to speedups of 453.8x and 200.9x over the measured CPU baseline.
conclusion: The study demonstrates implementation-specific throughput benefits from combining cryptographic precomputation, batched accelerator execution, and persistent runtime state, while distinguishing warm-batch performance from isolated-request latency.

title: Logics Of Filter Bubbles
authors: Jialiang Yan Lei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Filter bubbles can be understood as configurations characterized by within-group proximity and separation from outsiders. Personalized feeds may form or preserve such configurations. We develop hybrid-style logics for reasoning about filter bubbles. The static logic characterizes bubble-shaped configurations, while its dynamic extension captures their formation and persistence under personalized feeds. We provide sound and strongly complete axiomatizations for the static and dynamic logics and prove their decidability.
tldr: The paper develops hybrid-style modal logics to formally characterize filter-bubble configurations and their formation/persistence under personalized feeds.
motivation: Filter bubbles—social configurations marked by within-group proximity and separation from outsiders—are increasingly shaped by personalized recommendation feeds, yet lack a rigorous logical characterization.
method: The authors introduce a static hybrid logic capturing bubble-shaped configurations and a dynamic extension modeling how personalized feeds create and sustain them, then prove soundness, strong completeness, and decidability for both.
result: Sound and strongly complete axiomatizations are established for the static and dynamic logics, and decidability of the resulting systems is proven.
conclusion: The framework provides a formal logical foundation for reasoning about filter bubbles and their dynamics, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cipl: A Channel-Aware Framework For Recoverable Privacy Leakage In Llm Agents
authors: Tao Huang, Guosen Wu, Guolong Zheng, Jiayang Meng, Chen Hou, Xu Yang, Xuechao Yang, Feng Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy leakage in LLM agents is commonly evaluated within individual components such as memory, retrieval, or tool-use pipelines, which makes it difficult to distinguish internal exposure from information that an external observer can actually recover. We present CIPL (Channel Inversion for Privacy Leakage), a channel-aware evaluation framework for black-box privacy leakage in LLM agents. CIPL represents a target through sensitive source, selection, assembly, execution, observation, and extraction stages and evaluates the transition from selected sensitive units to attacker-recoverable output under a shared protocol. Experiments across memory-based, retrieval-mediated, and tool-mediated targets, together with a BrowserUse live-agent case study, show that storage labels alone do not determine recoverability. Memory targets form a near-saturated reference case, retrieval-mediated leakage is frequently partial, and tool-mediated and live-agent leakage varies strongly with observation surface, prompt-to-channel alignment, retrieval depth, and provider behavior. A stratified semantic audit further identifies attacker-useful disclosures that canonical exact matching misses. CIPL therefore provides a common framework for comparing how internal sensitive dependence is realized as externally recoverable leakage across heterogeneous agent pipelines.
tldr: CIPL is a channel-aware black-box evaluation framework for measuring recoverable privacy leakage in LLM agent pipelines.
motivation: Privacy leakage in LLM agents is typically assessed within isolated components, making it hard to separate internal sensitive exposure from information an external attacker can actually recover.
method: CIPL models a target through sensitive source, selection, assembly, execution, observation, and extraction stages, then evaluates the transition from selected sensitive units to attacker-recoverable output under a shared protocol across memory, retrieval, and tool-mediated targets plus a live-agent case study.
result: Experiments show that storage labels alone do not determine recoverability: memory targets form a near-saturated reference, retrieval-mediated leakage is often partial, and tool/live-agent leakage varies strongly with observation surface, prompt-to-channel alignment, retrieval depth, and provider behavior; a stratified semantic audit also finds attacker-useful disclosures missed by exact matching.
conclusion: CIPL offers a common framework for comparing how internal sensitive dependence becomes externally recoverable leakage across heterogeneous LLM agent pipelines.

title: Normal Forms And First Integrals Of Planar Maps At Elliptic Fixed Points
authors: Stavros Anastassiou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study real-analytic, planar, maps, at a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We construct normal forms for them, when they admit a real-analytic first integral. We prove that a second first integral, when it exists, forces their linearisation. We consider both the resonant and the non-resonant case, whether the maps preserve a symplectic form or not. The second first integral is allowed to be smooth, real-meromorphic or real-analytic.
tldr: The paper studies normal forms for real-analytic planar maps near elliptic fixed points when they admit a first integral, and shows that a second independent first integral forces linearisation.
motivation: Understanding integrability and normal forms of planar maps near elliptic fixed points is a classical problem in dynamical systems, with connections to symplectic geometry and Hamiltonian mechanics.
method: The authors construct normal forms for real-analytic planar maps with a real-analytic first integral, treating resonant and non-resonant cases, and analyze the consequences of a second first integral that may be smooth, real-meromorphic, or real-analytic.
result: They prove that the existence of a second first integral forces the map to be linearisable, regardless of whether the map preserves a symplectic form.
conclusion: The work advances the classical theory of normal forms and integrability for planar maps, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Robustness Analysis Via Horofunction Compactification
authors: Amin Farjudian Harrison Bennett
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robustness analysis plays a central role in the verification and design of computational and hybrid systems, particularly when system behaviour depends continuously on parameters subject to perturbation. Existing domain-theoretic frameworks provide a principled foundation for reasoning about such perturbations via monotone maps on lattices of closed sets. However, these frameworks face significant limitations when the underlying state space is not locally compact, as is the case for the infinite-dimensional spaces that arise in analysis, machine learning, and control theory (e.g., [MATH] and [MATH] spaces). In these settings, the lattice of closed subsets fails to be continuous, and classical compactifications either sacrifice precision or lack computable structure. We propose Gromov's horofunction compactification as a new tool for robustness analysis over a class of separable metric spaces of practical importance, including separable reflexive Banach spaces. Given a metric space [MATH], we show that its horofunction extension yields a compact metric space together with a Lipschitz embedding, which enables robust approximations of monotone maps via Scott-continuous maps on the compactified domain. For separable spaces, the horofunction compactification is metrizable, which provides a path toward effective domain-theoretic constructions.
tldr: The paper proposes Gromov's horofunction compactification as a domain-theoretic tool for robustness analysis of computational and hybrid systems over non-locally-compact separable metric spaces.
motivation: Existing domain-theoretic robustness frameworks rely on continuous lattices of closed sets, which break down when the state space is not locally compact (e.g., infinite-dimensional function spaces appearing in analysis, machine learning, and control theory).
method: The authors construct the horofunction extension of a separable metric space, showing it yields a compact metric space with a Lipschitz embedding, and use this to approximate monotone maps by Scott-continuous maps on the compactified domain.
result: For separable spaces, including separable reflexive Banach spaces, the horofunction compactification is metrizable, enabling effective domain-theoretic constructions and robust approximations that classical compactifications cannot provide.
conclusion: Horofunction compactification offers a principled route to robustness analysis in infinite-dimensional settings, opening a path toward computable, effective domain-theoretic verification of hybrid and continuous systems.

title: HE-Guardrail: A Homomorphic Guardrail Against Jailbreak Attacks For Encrypted Large Language Model Inference
authors: Byeongseo Min, Yongwoo Lee, Young-Sik Kim, Yongjune Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Homomorphic encryption (HE) has emerged as a promising approach to privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML), enabling computation directly over encrypted data. In HE-based PPML, a client submits an encrypted input to the server, which evaluates models such as large language models (LLMs) without access to the underlying plaintext. However, we identify a critical security vulnerability in this setting: HE-LLM inference is vulnerable to malicious clients that submit adversarial prompts, such as jailbreak attacks. The same confidentiality that protects benign clients also prevents the server from inspecting incoming prompts or generated responses, making adversarial attempts difficult to detect or block and potentially allowing successful attacks to remain entirely invisible to the server. To address this vulnerability, we propose HE-Guardrail, a framework that evaluates guardrail mechanisms entirely over encrypted data and homomorphically controls whether the target-model response is returned to the client. We instantiate HE-Guardrail with three representative guardrails - Llama Guard, JBShield, and GradSafe. Our results show that HE-Guardrail closely reproduces the decisions of the corresponding plaintext guardrails in the encrypted domain, with distinct security-efficiency-utility trade-offs.
tldr: HE-Guardrail is a framework for detecting jailbreak attacks in homomorphic-encryption-based LLM inference by evaluating guardrails entirely over encrypted data.
motivation: HE-based LLM inference protects client privacy but also prevents the server from inspecting prompts, creating a vulnerability to malicious jailbreak attacks that remain invisible to the server.
method: The authors design HE-Guardrail to homomorphically evaluate three representative guardrails—Llama Guard, JBShield, and GradSafe—and control whether the target model's response is returned to the client.
result: HE-Guardrail closely reproduces the decisions of plaintext guardrails in the encrypted domain while exposing distinct security-efficiency-utility trade-offs.
conclusion: The work highlights and mitigates a security gap in encrypted LLM inference, but remains outside the user's quantum information and thermodynamics research directions.

title: ServeGuard: Verifiable, Bounded-Residual Confinement Of Operator-Invisible Channels Without Revealing The Certified Read Factor
authors: Rui Vieira Dominik Dahlem
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third-party adapters for open-weight language models ship as opaque weight matrices; a recipient cannot check whether an adapter hides a backdoor without trusting the publisher or inspecting the weights, the publisher's core asset. For one important class (payloads placed where a safety monitor is structurally blind), detection is unsound as a defense: every detector that factors through the declared monitor is invariant on its blind subspace, and honest and backdoored adapters overlap on every blind-subspace statistic we evaluate, because benign adaptation uses that subspace too. Rather than detect this channel, we make it structurally and prove that we did. The publisher builds the adapter to read the input only through directions the monitor covers and proves this in zero knowledge, revealing nothing about the read factor it certifies. The certificate is cheap because the expensive part, identifying the monitor's blind spot, is a deterministic function of the base model, so only one linear identity is proved; the served residual is the base model's own public floor, not a prover-chosen tolerance. The result is , a supply-chain primitive: the publisher ships a whose proof lets a consumer or regulator verify, without the certified read factor and without trusting the publisher, that the adapter carries no hidden channel of this class relative to the declared monitor; an admission-time typing guard binds the guarantee to the adapter bytes admitted at serving time. Across eight checkpoints up to 7B from four families, the monitoring budget is architectural: the measured frontier saturates at the value-path rank on grouped-query checkpoints but not on multi-head ones. On a 0.5B model confinement is nearly free for benign adaptation, making monitor quality the security lever.
tldr: The paper introduces ServeGuard, a verifiable confinement mechanism that prevents third-party language-model adapters from hiding operator-invisible backdoor channels without revealing the certified read factor.
motivation: Opaque third-party adapters for open-weight language models can conceal backdoors, and detection is unsound for payloads placed in a safety monitor's structural blind spot.
method: The publisher constructs the adapter to read inputs only through directions the monitor covers, proves this property in zero knowledge, and binds the guarantee to the adapter bytes at serving time via an admission-time typing guard.
result: Across eight checkpoints up to 7B from four families, the monitoring budget is architectural; the measured frontier saturates at value-path rank on grouped-query checkpoints but not on multi-head ones, and confinement is nearly free for benign adaptation on a 0.5B model.
conclusion: ServeGuard provides a supply-chain primitive that lets consumers or regulators verify absence of this hidden-channel class relative to a declared monitor without trusting the publisher or learning the certified read factor.

title: Backward Log Orthogonal Functions And Their Approximation Theory
authors: Mahmoud A. Zaky
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new class of backward logarithmic orthogonal functions and generalized backward logarithmic orthogonal functions, constructed by applying a terminal-endpoint logarithmic mapping to generalized Laguerre polynomials. These functions are designed for backward spectral approximations of problems whose solutions exhibit weak singularities at the terminal endpoint. The proposed basis functions generate non-polynomial weighted approximation spaces with nodes naturally clustered near the singular endpoint, and therefore provide an effective framework for resolving algebraic and logarithmic endpoint singularities. We develop the basic approximation theory for these backward logarithmic orthogonal functions, including recurrence relations, derivative formulas, orthogonality, Sturm--Liouville characterization, mapped Laguerre--Gauss quadrature rules, weighted projection estimates, backward Lagrange interpolation estimates, inverse inequalities, and stability properties in weighted Sobolev-type spaces defined through a terminal logarithmic pseudo-derivative. A generalized version of the basis is also introduced by incorporating an algebraic scaling parameter, which improves the flexibility of the approximation space and allows singular factors to be represented more effectively. The error analysis and numerical results show that the proposed backward logarithmic basis is particularly suitable for weakly regular functions with terminal-endpoint singularities and can recover exponential or high-order convergence rates that are typically lost when usual polynomial approximations are applied directly.
tldr: The paper introduces backward logarithmic orthogonal functions, built from generalized Laguerre polynomials via a terminal-endpoint logarithmic mapping, for spectrally approximating solutions with weak endpoint singularities.
motivation: Standard polynomial approximations lose their exponential convergence when applied to weakly regular functions that exhibit algebraic or logarithmic singularities at a domain endpoint.
method: The authors construct new non-polynomial weighted bases by mapping generalized Laguerre polynomials through a terminal logarithmic transform, then derive recurrence relations, derivative and Sturm–Liouville formulas, quadrature rules, projection and interpolation error estimates, inverse inequalities, and stability results in weighted Sobolev-type spaces; a generalized version adds an algebraic scaling parameter.
result: The theoretical error analysis and numerical experiments show the basis recovers exponential or high-order convergence rates for functions with terminal-endpoint singularities, which conventional polynomial bases fail to achieve.
conclusion: The proposed backward logarithmic orthogonal functions provide an effective and flexible framework for backward spectral approximation of weakly singular problems, though the work lies in numerical analysis rather than quantum information science.

title: Exploiting Mutual Coupling Structure For Channel Estimation Of Active RIS-Assisted Links
authors: Simon Tarboush, Pinjun Zheng, Hadi Sarieddeen, Tareq Y. Al-Naffouri, Giuseppe Caire
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate channel modeling and estimation of active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted links with densely integrated elements are essential to fully unleashing this technology's potential. This work adopts a physically consistent model incorporating mutual coupling (MC) effects, modeled via scattering parameters, in RIS-aided communication. We formulate the MC-aware channel estimation as a compressed sensing (CS) problem. The MC effect leads to an increase in the sensing matrix dimensions. This increased dimensionality substantially elevates the complexity of the formulated CS problem. To overcome this, we propose a low-complexity estimator that leverages the structure of the scattering matrix and MC mechanisms to obtain a reduced-size design sensing matrix. Numerical results demonstrate that our approach outperforms MC-unaware estimators by several dBs, achieving accuracy comparable to fully MC-aware solutions but with significantly lower complexity.
tldr: The paper develops a low-complexity compressed-sensing channel estimator for active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted links that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling effects.
motivation: Accurate channel estimation for densely integrated active RIS elements is critical to realizing the technology's potential, yet mutual coupling between elements is typically ignored, biasing channel models.
method: The authors adopt a physically consistent scattering-parameter model of mutual coupling, cast MC-aware channel estimation as a compressed sensing problem, and exploit the structure of the scattering matrix to derive a reduced-dimension sensing matrix for a low-complexity estimator.
result: Numerical simulations show the proposed estimator outperforms MC-unaware baselines by several dB while matching fully MC-aware solutions at significantly lower computational complexity.
conclusion: Exploiting the mutual-coupling structure enables accurate, efficient channel estimation for active RIS-assisted links, bridging the gap between simplified and fully physical models.

title: Kernel-free Boundary Integral Methods For Allen-Cahn And Cahn-Hilliard Equations On Irregular Domains
authors: Xinru Liu, Pensong Yin, Wenjun Ying, Yulin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A unified kernel-free boundary integral (KFBI) framework is proposed for the Allen-Cahn and Cahn Hilliard equations with homogeneous no-flux boundary conditions on two- and three-dimensional irregular domains. With a stabilized first-order implici-explicit (IMEX) discretization, the Allen-Cahn update reduces to a Neumann modified Helmholtz problem. An auxiliary-variable reformulation reduces the Cahn-Hilliard update to subproblems of the same type without evaluating the Laplacian of the nonlinear source. The Cahn-Hilliard update requires two sequential solves for real shifts, while complex-conjugate shifts allow the real-valued solution to be reconstructed from a single complex solve. All subproblems are handled by the same KFBI solver that indirectly evaluates potentials through equivalent interface problems. To correct discrete mass defects in the Cahn-Hilliard update, a geometry-weighted discrete [MATH] mass projection is constructed tailored to the KFBI treatment of irregular boundaries. Exterior overlap weights are redistributed to physical nodes, excluding auxiliary KFBI extension values from the mass calculation. Numerical experiments demonstrate second-order spatial convergence, first order convergence of paired temporal-error indicators, and preservation of the prescribed discrete mass. The reported source-free simulations exhibit energy decay, with cumulative projection-induced energy perturbations remaining small relative to the observed dissipation.
tldr: The paper develops a unified kernel-free boundary integral framework for solving Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations on irregular domains with no-flux boundary conditions.
motivation: Nonlinear phase-field equations on irregular domains require accurate, stable numerical methods, particularly for homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions where standard finite-difference or spectral approaches face geometric complexities.
method: A stabilized first-order IMEX scheme reduces Allen-Cahn to a Neumann modified Helmholtz problem and Cahn-Hilliard to sequential shifted Helmholtz subproblems via an auxiliary-variable reformulation, all solved with a KFBI solver and a geometry-weighted discrete mass projection.
result: Numerical experiments show second-order spatial convergence, first-order temporal-error indicators, preservation of prescribed discrete mass, and small cumulative projection-induced energy perturbations relative to observed dissipation.
conclusion: The proposed KFBI framework provides an effective and accurate numerical tool for simulating Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard dynamics on irregular domains.

title: New Lower Bounds For Kissing Numbers In Dimensions $25$--$29$ And $31$
authors: Stanislav Yun Rustem Takhanov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The kissing number in dimension [MATH] is the largest number of non-overlapping congruent spheres that can simultaneously touch a central sphere of the same size. We study dimensions [MATH]-[MATH], where the best previous constructions are based on Leech lifting from the optimal kissing configuration in dimension [MATH]. Our method exploits the absence of contacts between the unlifted bulk and the block consisting of lifted and auxiliary vectors. Rotating this block while keeping the bulk fixed creates room for two antipodal points in dimensions [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], and one point in dimension [MATH]. Two further modifications yield improvements in dimensions [MATH] and [MATH]: a nonorthogonal diagonal linear deformation of the lifted block admits two antipodal points in dimension [MATH], while rotating only the additional coordinates of the lifted vectors admits four nonantipodal points in dimension [MATH]. Together, these constructions yield the new lower bounds [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH].
tldr: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 25–29 and 31 are constructed by rotating and deforming the Leech-lifted block while keeping the bulk fixed.
motivation: Kissing numbers in dimensions above 24 are poorly understood, with the best previous constructions relying on Leech lifting from dimension 24, leaving room for incremental improvements in a few intermediate dimensions.
method: The authors exploit the absence of contacts between the unlifted bulk and the lifted/auxiliary block, then rotate the block and apply a nonorthogonal diagonal linear deformation to admit additional antipodal or nonantipodal contact points.
result: The constructions yield improved lower bounds in dimensions 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, and 31, with two antipodal points added in dimensions 25, 26, and 28, one in 27, two via diagonal deformation in 29, and four nonantipodal points in 31.
conclusion: The work advances the classical combinatorial geometry of sphere packing and kissing configurations, but has no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Compact Partial Symmetry Breaking For Graph Search Problems
authors: Michael Codish, Mikol\'{a}\v{s} Janota, Peter J. Stuckey
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry breaking in graph search problems remains challenging: complete symmetry breaking constraints are typically exponential in size, while partial approaches trade precision for scalability. We introduce a strength-driven, redundancy-aware methodology for constructing compact partial symmetry breaking constraints based on graph patterns. Each pattern corresponds to a Boolean clause over equality literals and can be integrated directly into CP or SAT models. Our approach incrementally selects strong, non-redundant graph patterns, yielding partial symmetry breaks that achieve substantial pruning of non-canonical graphs while remaining compact in size. This provides a principled framework for deriving lightweight partial symmetry breaking constraints which are significantly more precise than all published state-of-the-art alternatives. We evaluate the proposed constraints on graph instances with up to 25 vertices using a redundancy ratio metric. The resulting partial symmetry breaks constitute only a small fraction of the size of complete symmetry breaking constraints, while delivering significant performance improvements across several graph search benchmarks compared to previously defined partial symmetry breaking methods.
tldr: The paper introduces a compact partial symmetry breaking methodology for graph search problems using strength-driven, redundancy-aware graph pattern constraints integrated into CP or SAT models.
motivation: Complete symmetry breaking constraints are often exponentially large, while existing partial methods sacrifice precision; the authors aim to derive compact yet powerful partial symmetry breaks.
method: They select strong, non-redundant graph patterns corresponding to Boolean clauses over equality literals, incrementally building partial symmetry breaking constraints for CP/SAT solvers.
result: On graph instances up to 25 vertices, the constraints are much smaller than complete symmetry breaking constraints and significantly outperform prior partial symmetry breaking methods in pruning and search performance.
conclusion: The approach provides a principled framework for lightweight partial symmetry breaking that is more precise and scalable than existing alternatives.

title: Generation Of Stable Peak-Power Similaritons Through Gain-Managed Nonlinearity
authors: Haoyuan He, Maksim Kozlov, Alexander Gabriel Loehr, Peng Gao, Misha Ivanov, Pavel Sidorenko
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fiber lasers and amplifiers offer attractive alternatives to conventional solid-state systems. However, generation of high-energy ultrashort laser pulses in fibers faces challenges due to the complex interplay of multiple nonlinear effects arising due to pulse confinement within a small fiber core and also limitations imposed by the gain bandwidth of the available active fibers. The discovery of self-similar amplification and gain-managed nonlinear amplification (GMNA) pulse propagation regimes in fibers with normal dispersion suggests that these challenges can be turned into an advantage. Here we show that pulses generated in the GMNA regime are, in fact, the realization of the idealized similariton-type pulses in realistic fibers with limited gain bandwidth. Our analytical and numerical results show how one should shape the fiber gain as a function of propagation length to achieve constant peak power similariton-like pulses with steadily increasing energy, the pulse bandwidth exceeding the gain bandwidth, and the nearly linear frequency chirp allowing for efficient pulse compression to its Fourier limit. Absent Raman nonlinearities, these pulses can reach [MATH]J level energies in standard single-mode fibers, representing a tenfold increase in pulse energy compared to the best currently available nonlinear amplifiers. Our results have significant implications for the fundamental understanding of nonlinear wave dynamics and for the advancement of fiber laser technology, supporting the reliable generation of high-energy pulses for practical use in areas such as micromachining, metrology, and bioimaging.
tldr: The paper analyzes gain-managed nonlinear amplification in fiber lasers and shows that it realizes idealized similariton pulses with stable peak power and compressible bandwidth.
motivation: Fiber amplifiers are attractive for high-energy ultrashort pulses but suffer from nonlinearities and gain-bandwidth limitations; self-similar and gain-managed regimes may overcome these constraints.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical modeling of pulse propagation in normal-dispersion fibers to determine how fiber gain should vary with propagation length to achieve similariton-like pulses.
result: The pulses maintain constant peak power while energy grows, exhibit bandwidth exceeding the gain bandwidth, and have nearly linear chirp suitable for compression to the Fourier limit.
conclusion: GMNA pulses can reach microjoule-level energies in standard single-mode fibers, enabling high-energy pulse generation for micromachining, metrology, and bioimaging.

title: Learning-based Near- Versus Far-field Boundaries For Ultra-massive Mimo Communications
authors: Simon Tarboush, Nour Kouzayha, Hadi Sarieddeen, Tareq Y. Al-Naffouri, Giuseppe Caire
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Signal processing techniques for wireless communications and sensing fundamentally differ between near-field and far-field propagation regimes. Accurately identifying the applicable propagation region is therefore essential for enabling efficient beamforming and channel estimation in ultra-massive MIMO (UM-MIMO) systems. This paper proposes a fully unsupervised learning framework to distinguish near-field from far-field propagation based solely on received signal measurements, before estimating the communication distance, and without relying on channel state information. The proposed approach exploits spatial signal power variations across subarrays of a UM array as a physics-inspired feature extraction stage, followed by the OPTICS clustering algorithm to infer the communication region. Simulation results under various system configurations and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels demonstrate that the proposed method accurately identifies the near-field and far-field regions, showing agreement with theoretical boundaries.
tldr: This paper proposes an unsupervised learning framework to distinguish near-field from far-field propagation regions in ultra-massive MIMO systems using received signal measurements without channel state information.
motivation: Accurate identification of the propagation region is essential for efficient beamforming and channel estimation in ultra-massive MIMO systems, but conventional methods require channel state information or prior distance estimates.
method: The approach extracts physics-inspired features from spatial signal power variations across subarrays of a UM array and applies OPTICS clustering to infer the communication region and estimate distance.
result: Simulations under various system configurations and SNR levels show accurate identification of near-field and far-field regions, matching theoretical boundaries.
conclusion: The proposed fully unsupervised method enables robust propagation-region classification without CSI, benefiting beamforming and channel estimation in UM-MIMO systems.

title: Performance Analysis Of Cooperative Multi-Carrier Relay-Based Uav Networks Over Generalized Fading Channels
authors: Mustafa M. Matalgah Ibrahim Y. Abualhaol
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The outage probability in a network of cooperative unmanned airborne vehicles (UAVs) over generalized fading channels is studied analytically using finite mixture with expectation maximization technique. A relay-based topology with one ground control unit (GCU) is considered, where the cooperative UAVs can communicate with the GCU directly or through relay. The application the UAV assigned for specifies the minimum required transmission rate the UAV should achieve. The outage probability of the system is defined as the probability that either the transmission rate over any of the links drops below a predefined minimum threshold for that link or the Relay-GCU link is not able to transmit the aggregate data from all relayed UAVs and the minimum rate required by the relay UAV itself. Throughout the paper, expressions for the outage probability and the average achievable bit rate of a cooperative multi-carrier system are derived over generalized fading channels. Finite Mixture with Expectation-Maximization algorithm is utilized to derive a simple approximate expression for the probability density function (pdf) of the achievable bit rate assuming adaptive M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (M-QAM). This pdf is used to derive closed-form expressions for the outage probability and the average bit rate.
tldr: The paper analyzes outage probability and average achievable bit rate for cooperative multi-carrier relay-based UAV networks over generalized fading channels.
motivation: Cooperative UAV networks require reliable communication links, and performance analysis over realistic fading channels is needed to design and evaluate such systems.
method: The authors use a finite mixture with expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm to approximate the probability density function of the achievable bit rate under adaptive M-QAM, and derive closed-form expressions for outage probability and average bit rate.
result: Closed-form expressions for outage probability and average achievable bit rate are obtained for a relay-based topology with one ground control unit, considering direct and relayed links.
conclusion: The proposed analytical framework provides a simple and accurate way to evaluate the performance of cooperative UAV networks under generalized fading conditions.

title: The Kadets--Werner Modification Of Bourgain--Rosenthal Space Is Asymptotically Midpoint Uniformly Convex
authors: Florent P. Baudier
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the Kadets--Werner modification of a closed subspace of [MATH] constructed by Bourgain and Rosenthal in 1980. In this short note, it is shown that [MATH] is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex. Since [MATH] has the Daugavet Property, it fails the Point of Continuity Property and thus does not admit an equivalent norm that is asymptotically uniformly convex. Therefore, the previously known properties of [MATH] and the new geometric observation answer, in the negative, the question of Dilworth, Kutzarova, Randrianarivony, Revalski and Zhivkov whether asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity and asymptotic uniform convexity are isomorphically equivalent and a question of Perreau whether asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity implies the Point of Continuity Property.
tldr: This short note proves that the Kadets--Werner modification of a Bourgain--Rosenthal space is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex, answering two open questions in Banach space geometry.
motivation: The paper addresses whether asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity and asymptotic uniform convexity are isomorphically equivalent, and whether asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity implies the Point of Continuity Property.
method: It uses geometric Banach space techniques to show that a specific Kadets--Werner modification is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex, and combines this with known properties of the space.
result: The space is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex but fails the Point of Continuity Property and does not admit an equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm.
conclusion: This resolves in the negative the question of Dilworth et al. on isomorphic equivalence and Perreau's question on the Point of Continuity Property.

title: History-Compatible Energy-Stable Finite Element Schemes For Variable-Density Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes Flows On Evolving Meshes
authors: Wenbin Wang, Yunqing Huang, Yin Yang, Huayi Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider variable-density Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes (CHNS) discretizations on finite element meshes that may change between accepted time levels through fixed-topology motion or topology-changing remeshing. When the discrete spaces vary in time, the phase, kinetic, and pressure histories entering a multistep scheme are measured in different discrete structures and cannot, in general, be transferred by a single operator. We develop decoupled backward Euler (BE) and second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2) schemes by combining exact physical cross-mesh pairings with history representations compatible with the corresponding phase-energy, kinetic-energy, and pressure-gradient storages. The phase update also determines an Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un-consistent mass flux used in the momentum transport. A scalar capillary-exchange equation separates the phase and fluid solves while retaining the discrete energy exchange. The resulting field subproblems are linear, the scalar equation has a unique positive solution, and the schemes satisfy modified energy balances without a time-step restriction under the stated admissibility assumptions. Numerical experiments confirm second-order temporal convergence under both mesh updates, phase-mass conservation, modified-energy decay in the unforced tests, and comparable Rayleigh--Taylor and rising-bubble dynamics.
tldr: The paper develops decoupled backward Euler and BDF2 finite element schemes for variable-density Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes flows on meshes that may change between time steps, preserving discrete energy stability and phase-mass conservation.
motivation: Simulating variable-density two-phase flows on evolving or remeshed finite element meshes is challenging because the discrete spaces change in time, so history variables stored in previous discrete structures cannot be transferred by a single operator without breaking energy stability.
method: The authors introduce history-compatible representations of phase, kinetic, and pressure histories together with exact physical cross-mesh pairings, an Abels-Garcke-Grun-consistent mass flux, and a scalar capillary-exchange equation that decouples the phase and fluid solves while retaining discrete energy exchange.
result: The resulting schemes are linear, the scalar equation has a unique positive solution, and the schemes satisfy modified energy balances without time-step restrictions under stated admissibility assumptions; numerical experiments confirm second-order temporal convergence, phase-mass conservation, and modified-energy decay.
conclusion: The proposed schemes provide a robust framework for energy-stable, second-order accurate simulation of variable-density CHNS flows on both moving and remeshed finite element meshes.

title: A Sparse Corner-Difference Milp For Minimum Square Tiling
authors: Zhuo Yu (shenzhen Research Institute Of Big Data, Shenzhen, China, The Chinese University Of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, China), Yuan Wang (shenzhen Research Institute Of Big Data, Shenzhen, China, The Chinese University Of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, China), Zhuo Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of tiling an [MATH] square with axis-aligned squares whose side lengths are integers strictly less than [MATH], with the objective of minimizing the number of tiles. The standard placement-based exact-cover MILP contains [MATH] placement-to-cell nonzero coefficients and is also affected by the dihedral symmetry of the square domain. We introduce a Corner-Difference MILP (CD-MILP) that represents each selected square by at most four signed corner coefficients. Two-dimensional prefix reconstruction shows that the resulting constraints are equivalent to the original cell-cover equations, while reducing the coverage-related nonzero count to [MATH]. We also introduce lightweight corner-ordering constraints that retain at least one representative from every [MATH] orbit, although ties may leave residual symmetry. Computational experiments on nine prime-size instances compare the baseline, CD-MILP, the baseline with corner ordering, and their combination using Gurobi and COPT. Under the stated experimental settings, the combined formulation solves eight instances with Gurobi and seven with COPT, compared with four and five, respectively, for the baseline. Its average presolved matrixs contain approximately [MATH] nonzero coefficients on average, compared with approximately [MATH] for the baseline.
tldr: This paper introduces a Corner-Difference MILP formulation for minimizing the number of integer-sided squares tiling an MxM square, reducing nonzero coefficients and symmetry issues compared to a standard placement-based exact-cover MILP.
motivation: The standard placement-based exact-cover MILP for minimum square tiling has many nonzero coefficients and is affected by dihedral symmetry, so a more efficient formulation is desired.
method: The authors propose a Corner-Difference MILP that represents each selected square by at most four signed corner coefficients, using two-dimensional prefix reconstruction to maintain equivalence. They also add lightweight corner-ordering constraints to partially break symmetry.
result: On nine prime-size instances, the combined formulation solved eight instances with Gurobi and seven with COPT, compared to four and five for the baseline, and presolved matrices had approximately fewer nonzeros on average.
conclusion: The CD-MILP improves computational performance for exact minimum square tiling, though residual symmetry may remain due to ties.

title: A Priori And A Posteriori Error Estimates For A Crank Nicolson Type Scheme Of An Elliptic Problem With Dynamical Boundary Conditions
authors: Rola Ali Ahmad, Toufic El Arwadi, Houssam Chrayteh, Jean-Marc Sac-\'ep\'ee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we claim that we are going to give a priori and a posteriori error estimates for a Crank Nicolson type scheme. The problem is discretized by the finite elements in space. The main result of this paper consists in establishing two types of error indicators, the first one linked to the time discretization and the second one to the space discretization.
tldr: The paper derives a priori and a posteriori error estimates for a Crank-Nicolson-type finite element discretization of an elliptic problem with dynamical boundary conditions.
motivation: Numerical schemes for problems with dynamical boundary conditions require rigorous error control to guarantee accuracy and guide adaptive refinement.
method: The problem is discretized using finite elements in space and a Crank-Nicolson-type time-stepping scheme, and two error indicators are derived—one for temporal and one for spatial discretization.
result: Two types of error indicators are established, separating the contributions of time discretization and space discretization, and corresponding a priori and a posteriori bounds are proven.
conclusion: The proposed estimators provide a rigorous framework for error control and adaptivity in this class of elliptic problems with dynamical boundary conditions.

title: Integral Chemical Reaction Neural Networks
authors: Stefan G\"uttel Abraham Reyes-Vel\'azquez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discovering the structure and kinetics of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) from time-series concentration data is a fundamental challenge in chemical kinetics, with existing approaches relying on prior mechanistic assumptions or suffering from high computational cost and noise sensitivity. In this work, we present integral chemical reaction neural networks (iCRNNs), a framework that combines the interpretable, physics-constrained, architecture of chemical reaction neural networks (CRNNs) with an integral collocation formulation of the governing dynamics. Rather than solving ODEs forward in time at each training step, we approximate the integral of the learned rate functions directly using numerical quadrature. This yields an entirely algebraic forward pass consisting only of matrix operations, eliminating the repeated adaptive ODE solves of standard CRNN and producing smoother, more predictable training. We provide a recovery error analysis characterising the structural sources of ill-conditioning (conservation laws, reaction reversibility, and shared reactant sets) that limit network identifiability. On two benchmark CRNs, iCRNN trains in roughly half the wall-clock time of the baseline CRNN method on a four-species mechanism and between three and four times faster on a five-species mechanism, while completing every training run reliably and attaining comparable or lower loss.
tldr: iCRNNs combine physics-constrained chemical reaction neural networks with integral collocation to efficiently discover chemical reaction networks from concentration time-series data.
motivation: Existing methods for inferring chemical reaction network structure and kinetics rely on prior mechanistic assumptions or suffer from high computational cost and noise sensitivity.
method: The framework approximates the integral of learned rate functions via numerical quadrature, replacing repeated ODE solves with an algebraic forward pass, and includes a recovery error analysis of ill-conditioning sources.
result: iCRNN trains roughly twice as fast as baseline CRNN on a four-species mechanism and three to four times faster on a five-species mechanism, with comparable or lower loss and reliable training runs.
conclusion: The work provides an efficient interpretable method for chemical kinetics discovery, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Finite Volume Element Method On Curved-Edge Meshes
authors: Xiaoxiao Chen, Zexi Hu, Zhiming Gao, Junliang Lv, Xiang Wang, Hongtao Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a high-order finite volume element method on curved-edge quadrilateral meshes for elliptic equations. Unlike existing theories, which are primarily based on straight-edge meshes, this study is the first to establish an analysis of the stability and optimal convergence of the finite volume method on curved-edge meshes. By constructing a dual mesh based on Gaussian points, we overcome the accuracy degradation issues caused by geometric deformation and Jacobian non-uniformity of curved-edge meshes. We prove the coercivity of the discrete bilinear form under weak mesh regularity conditions, thereby obtaining an optimal error estimate in the energy norm. Furthermore, using orthogonality and the Aubin-Nitsche technique, we derive an optimal [MATH] error estimate. Numerical experiments cover problems with constant and anisotropic coefficients, different dual partition strategies, complex curved boundary domains, and interfaces with large deformations. Numerical results indicate that this method consistently achieves the optimal convergence order in both the [MATH] and [MATH] norms on a variety of curved-edge meshes. Compared to straight-edge meshes, curved-edge meshes offer significant advantages in approximating complex curved boundaries and demonstrate better resistance to distortion in cases involving sudden changes in coefficients and large deformations at interfaces. This paper provides a unified theoretical framework for the finite volume element method on curved-edge meshes and verifies the efficiency and robustness of the proposed method.
tldr: The paper develops and analyzes a high-order finite volume element method on curved-edge quadrilateral meshes for elliptic equations, establishing stability and optimal convergence results.
motivation: Existing finite volume element theories are primarily developed for straight-edge meshes, limiting accuracy on complex curved boundaries and deformed interfaces.
method: A dual mesh constructed from Gaussian points is introduced to mitigate geometric deformation and Jacobian non-uniformity, and coercivity of the discrete bilinear form is proven under weak mesh regularity conditions.
result: Optimal energy-norm and L2 error estimates are derived via orthogonality and the Aubin-Nitsche technique, and numerical experiments confirm optimal convergence for constant/anisotropic coefficients, complex curved domains, and large-deformation interfaces.
conclusion: The work offers a unified theoretical framework for finite volume element methods on curved-edge meshes and demonstrates their robustness and boundary-approximation advantages over straight-edge meshes.

title: The Right Tool For The Job: On The Selection Of Mitigations For GenAI Privacy Threats
authors: Jonah Bellemans, Qianying Liao, Laurens Sion, Lieven Desmet, Wouter Joosen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has rapidly evolved from an experimental technology into a foundational component of modern software systems. However, as its adoption grows, protecting sensitive personal data becomes increasingly challenging. Specifically, GenAI systems not only amplify traditional privacy threats but also introduce new inference-based risks, such as constructing detailed user profiles from seemingly harmless inputs. In response, privacy threat modeling frameworks are beginning to capture GenAI-specific privacy threats with finer granularity. At the same time, a growing number of mitigation techniques have been proposed to address these threats. However, although knowledge of both threats and mitigations continues to mature, the problem- and solution-space have developed largely independently. This position paper argues that the primary challenge in GenAI privacy engineering is not the lack of knowledge about privacy threats or mitigation techniques, but the missing bridge between them. We decompose this gap into three sub-problems: (i) lack of fine-grained threat-to-mitigation mapping for GenAI systems, (ii) inapplicable solution-space assumptions in the GenAI context, and (iii) prioritization difficulty under GenAI constraints. We derive four recommendations for future mitigation-selection approaches, and outline a suggested approach that extends established threat-to-mitigation mapping methods to GenAI-specific threat characteristics. We propose a research agenda toward more systematic privacy mitigation selection for GenAI-based systems.
tldr: A position paper arguing that GenAI privacy engineering lacks a systematic bridge between GenAI-specific privacy threats and available mitigation techniques.
motivation: GenAI systems amplify traditional privacy risks and introduce new inference-based threats, while mitigation knowledge is growing—yet threat modeling and mitigation research have developed independently.
method: The authors decompose the threat-to-mitigation gap into three sub-problems (missing fine-grained threat-to-mitigation mapping, inapplicable solution-space assumptions, prioritization difficulty) and derive four recommendations, outlining an approach extending established mapping methods to GenAI threat characteristics.
result: No empirical results; the paper identifies structural gaps in GenAI privacy engineering and proposes a research agenda for systematic mitigation selection.
conclusion: The main challenge is not a lack of knowledge about GenAI privacy threats or mitigations but the missing connection between them, motivating future work on systematic mitigation-selection approaches.

title: (Don't) Trust, But (Don't) Verify: Developers' Attention To Security In AI-Generated Code
authors: Hamza Khalid, Ronald E. Thompson III, Alejandra Sabater, Perucy Mussiba, Kelsey R. Fulton, Daniel Votipka
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding assistants are rapidly transforming software development, but are known to produce insecure code. Prior work has measured whether AI-assisted developers produce secure code, but less is known about how they evaluate AI-generated code: whether they can identify vulnerabilities, what cues they use, and how trust shapes their decisions. This evaluation step is foundational to secure development with AI, whether using auto-complete, chat tools, or AI agents. As a first step, we conducted a remote observational study with 100 participants isolating this evaluation stage. Participants were tasked with producing secure and functional code for four C linked-list tasks. For each, participants were able to cycle through five AI-generated suggestions varying in security and functionality, select one, and edit their choice into a final submission. Participants also completed a post-study survey about their decision-making and perception of AI-generated code's security and 23 completed a more in-depth interview.
tldr: A remote observational study with 100 developers examines how they evaluate AI-generated code for security, including vulnerability identification, cues used, and the influence of trust.
motivation: AI coding assistants often produce insecure code, but less is known about how developers assess AI-generated code before accepting it, which is critical for secure AI-assisted development.
method: Participants completed four C linked-list tasks by cycling through five AI-generated suggestions of varying security and functionality, selecting and editing one, then completing a survey; 23 also participated in in-depth interviews.
result: The study reveals developers' attention patterns, vulnerability detection abilities, decision cues, and how trust shapes their security-related choices when evaluating AI-generated code.
conclusion: Understanding developer evaluation of AI-generated code is foundational for secure development with AI, highlighting gaps in trust and verification practices.

title: Origin Is All You Need: Provenance-Aware Transformers For Structural Trust-Boundary Separation
authors: Yuxuan Zhang, Jeff Huang, Guofei Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indirect prompt injection (IPI) remains a central safety and security challenge for large language model (LLM) systems because standard transformers lack architectural notion of source authority. Retrieved documents, user inputs, and system instructions are all processed through the same undifferentiated attention mechanism, forcing the model to infer from wording alone what should be obeyed and what should be treated as data. We propose Provenance-Aware Transformers, a provenance-aware defense that makes application-supplied source labels actionable inside the model. Each input token is assigned a ring ID encoding its origin, and the model is augmented with origin embeddings, a learnable origin attention bias, and a learnable origin scale that preserves provenance under normalization. The resulting architecture enforces a structural boundary between authoritative and non-authoritative sources during generation. To instantiate this architecture on released pretrained models, we propose a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline to teach the model origin semantics and task behavior under ring constraints. Evaluation shows that Provenance-Aware Transformers maintain robust resistance to IPI both in-distribution and out-of-distribution while preserving utility comparable to the base pretrained model. More broadly, our work shows that exposing provenance as a first-class architectural signal can shift LLM safety alignment from brittle pattern matching toward explicit trust separation.
tldr: The paper proposes Provenance-Aware Transformers, an architecture that encodes token origin (ring IDs, origin embeddings, attention biases) to structurally separate authoritative from non-authoritative sources and defend LLMs against indirect prompt injection.
motivation: Standard transformers have no architectural notion of source authority, so retrieved documents, user inputs, and system instructions compete in the same undifferentiated attention mechanism, leaving indirect prompt injection a persistent safety vulnerability.
method: Each input token is assigned a ring ID encoding provenance; the model is augmented with origin embeddings, a learnable origin attention bias, and a learnable origin scale that preserves provenance under normalization, instantiated on pretrained LLMs via a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline.
result: Provenance-Aware Transformers maintain robust in-distribution and out-of-distribution resistance to indirect prompt injection while preserving utility comparable to the base pretrained model.
conclusion: Exposing provenance as a first-class architectural signal shifts LLM safety alignment from brittle pattern matching toward explicit trust-boundary separation between authoritative and non-authoritative sources.

title: X-spur: Explainable Surprisal-Based Protocol-Aware Unsupervised Reasoning For Automotive Ethernet Intrusion Detection
authors: Seonghoon Jeong Jisoo Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automotive Ethernet carries heterogeneous multi-protocol traffic in modern in-vehicle networks, where labeled attack data are rarely available and the strongest prior unsupervised detector still relies on handcrafted traffic features. This article presents X-SPUR, an explainable, surprisal-based, protocol-aware unsupervised reasoning framework that instead represents raw packet fields as token sequences, learns benign traffic patterns through causal language modeling, and detects anomalies from per-token cross-entropy surprisal.
