To incorporate temporal context, we introduce a bimodal fusion architecture that combines payload-token embeddings with inter-packet timing through additive fusion and a Hadamard interaction. To handle the heterogeneous score distributions of different protocol families, we further propose a dual top-[MATH]% per-protocol [MATH]-score calibration that jointly captures moderately distributed and sparse anomaly signatures. On the TOW-IDS dataset, X-SPUR achieves an AUC of 0.9987. This is marginally higher than the 0.9969 reported for AERO. X-SPUR also eliminates handcrafted feature engineering. We train a separate CarDS model using the same architecture and training hyperparameters. This model retains strong performance on the second automotive Ethernet dataset. Beyond detection, per-token surprisal provides fine-grained explainability by attributing anomaly scores to specific protocol fields, supporting interpretable security analysis in heterogeneous in-vehicle networks.
tldr: X-SPUR is an explainable, surprisal-based, protocol-aware unsupervised anomaly detection framework for automotive Ethernet that models raw packet fields as token sequences via causal language modeling.
motivation: Automotive Ethernet carries heterogeneous multi-protocol traffic where labeled attack data are scarce, and existing unsupervised detectors rely on handcrafted traffic features that are brittle and uninterpretable.
method: Raw packet fields are tokenized and modeled with causal language modeling to learn benign traffic patterns; anomaly scores come from per-token cross-entropy surprisal, with a bimodal fusion of payload embeddings and inter-packet timing plus dual top-M% per-protocol calibration.
result: X-SPUR achieves AUC 0.9987 on TOW-IDS, marginally exceeding AERO's 0.9969, eliminates handcrafted feature engineering, and generalizes to a second dataset (CarDS) with strong performance.
conclusion: The framework shows that surprisal-based language modeling can deliver state-of-the-art, interpretable intrusion detection for in-vehicle networks without manual feature design.

title: TrustBOM: A Scalable Architecture For Confidentiality-Preserving SBOMs Across Organizations
authors: van Thang Nguyen, Frederic Rupprecht, Tom Lawrence, Lucca Di Benedetto, S\"oren Schubert, Amor Rezgui, Sebastian Werner, Maria C. Borges, Stefan Tai
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) have emerged as a key mechanism for software supply chain governance in enterprise architectures. However, their adoption across organizations remains limited due to concerns about exposing sensitive dependency information. To address this limitation, we propose TrustBOM, a scalable architecture for confidentiality-preserving SBOMs integrated into enterprise CI/CD workflows. TrustBOM enables software providers to attest that specific vulnerabilities or restricted licenses are absent from their software without revealing the underlying dependency graph. This is achieved using zero-knowledge non-membership proofs, which are applied selectively based on consumer-defined policy constraints. The architecture ensures that proof generation scales linearly with the number of asserted constraints rather than with the size of the SBOM, enabling efficient operation in large-scale enterprise environments. Empirical evaluation demonstrates linear performance, with an average proof generation time of 0.9 seconds per constraint on commodity hardware, indicating the feasibility of deployment in enterprise platform ecosystems.
tldr: TrustBOM is a scalable architecture for confidentiality-preserving SBOMs using zero-knowledge non-membership proofs to hide dependency graphs while attesting absence of vulnerabilities or restricted licenses.
motivation: SBOM adoption across organizations is limited by concerns over exposing sensitive dependency information, which hinders software supply chain governance.
method: The architecture employs zero-knowledge non-membership proofs applied selectively based on consumer-defined policy constraints, with proof generation scaling linearly with the number of asserted constraints rather than SBOM size.
result: Empirical evaluation shows linear performance with an average proof generation time of 0.9 seconds per constraint on commodity hardware.
conclusion: TrustBOM demonstrates feasibility for deployment in enterprise CI/CD workflows, enabling confidential SBOM verification without revealing the underlying dependency graph.

title: Defeat: Stitching Fragmented File I/o Contexts For Early Ransomware Detection
authors: Muhammad Ejaz Ahmed, Hyoungshick Kim, Mohsen Ali Alawami, Alsharif Abuadbba, Seyit Camtepe, Surya Nepal, Junaid Qadir
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ransomware increasingly fragments its file operations across temporary and intermediate files, scattering the semantic context that links individual I/O events to an overarching encryption campaign. This fragmentation defeats existing detectors that reason over isolated file streams -- whether pattern-based methods that match rigid event sequences or learning-based methods that require accumulating statistical evidence across many files. We present DEFEAT, a framework that reconstructs this fragmented, scattered context by grouping causally related file events into File Event Gadgets (FEGs), semantically coherent units that capture the full intent behind sequences of file operations spanning multiple dynamically created files. Unlike provenance graphs (system-wide causal graphs that record relationships among all OS entities, such as processes, files, sockets, and registry keys, across the entire system), FEGs are scoped to the file-operation context of a single user asset, enabling lightweight, targeted analysis without whole-system instrumentation. Each FEG is modelled as an attributed control flow graph (ACFG) and embedded via a graph neural network for unsupervised clustering, enabling analysts to label entire behavioural clusters rather than individual samples, reducing annotation effort by 94%. Evaluated on a corpus of 97,816,471 file I/O events spanning 67 ransomware families, DEFEAT achieves 99.2% detection accuracy and outperforms state-of-the-art methods including UNVEIL, RWGuard, and Peeler by 6.57 to 7.56%. The framework operates at the granularity of a single file encryption: because each ACFG represents exactly one FEG (one user asset context), a cluster label can be assigned as soon as the first file operation completes, enabling detection at the first encrypted file.
tldr: DEFEAT is a ransomware detection framework that reconstructs fragmented file I/O contexts into File Event Gadgets (FEGs) and clusters them via graph neural networks for early detection.
motivation: Ransomware increasingly fragments file operations across temporary and intermediate files, defeating existing detectors that analyze isolated file streams or require accumulating evidence across many files.
method: The framework groups causally related file events into semantically coherent FEGs scoped to a single user asset, models each as an attributed control flow graph (ACFG), and embeds them with a graph neural network for unsupervised clustering.
result: Evaluated on 97,816,471 file I/O events from 67 ransomware families, DEFEAT achieves 99.2% detection accuracy and outperforms UNVEIL, RWGuard, and Peeler by 6.57–7.56%, while reducing annotation effort by 94%.
conclusion: By detecting at the granularity of a single file encryption and enabling cluster-level labeling, DEFEAT provides lightweight, early ransomware detection without whole-system instrumentation.

title: Micro-Collaborative Poisoning: A Distributed Attack On Rag Systems
authors: Pedro Pereira, Eva Maia, Isabel Pra\c{c}a
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves large language models by grounding outputs in external knowledge sources, but this dependency also creates a surface for poisoning attacks. This paper introduces Micro-Collaborative Poisoning, a distributed attack in which a false target claim is divided across multiple locally plausible documents instead of being concentrated in a single malicious passage. We evaluate the attack across 108 RAG configurations by varying dataset, retriever architecture, retrieval depth, database composition, number of poisoned databases, and generator model. The results indicate that Micro-Collaborative Poisoning is not driven by a single dominant poisoned passage, but by the accumulation of weak adversarial signals across retrieved sources. Increasing top-[MATH] and poisoning multiple databases make it more likely that these signals will appear together in the retrieved context, while clean database diversity and stronger retrievers can reduce their influence. The document-level poisoning visibility analysis further shows that this threat is difficult to expose through isolated document inspection, since Micro-Collaborative Poisoning achieves downstream influence while leaving a weaker explicit poisoning signature than direct poisoning.
tldr: Introduces Micro-Collaborative Poisoning, a distributed attack that spreads false claims across multiple plausible documents to manipulate Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems.
motivation: RAG systems rely on external knowledge retrieval, creating a vulnerability where poisoned documents can influence outputs; existing poisoning attacks often concentrate malicious content in a single passage.
method: The attack splits a false target claim across many locally plausible documents, then evaluates its effectiveness across 108 RAG configurations by varying datasets, retrievers, retrieval depths, database composition, number of poisoned databases, and generator models.
result: Attack success arises from accumulated weak adversarial signals across retrieved sources rather than a single dominant passage; increasing retrieval depth and poisoning multiple databases increase influence, while clean database diversity and stronger retrievers reduce it.
conclusion: Micro-Collaborative Poisoning is difficult to detect via isolated document inspection because it exerts downstream influence with a weaker explicit poisoning signature than direct poisoning.

title: Integration Of The Nist Spectroscopic Plate Archive Into The Harvard Plate Stacks
authors: Jacob Ward, Thom Burns, Lisa Bravata, Gillian Nave, Adam Foster
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For many decades, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Atomic Spectroscopy Group housed a growing collection of thousands of photographic glass plate negatives. With the closure of the NIST Atomic Spectroscopy Group in March 2025, the irreplaceable collection needed a new home. Staff from NIST were contacted by staff from the Harvard Plate Stacks at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian (CfA). The Harvard Plate Stacks is the largest collection of astronomical glass plates in the world, with over 500,000 glass plate negatives from the 1880s to the 1990s. Given the long-standing history of the Harvard Plate Stacks and the expertise of the staff, it was decided that the NIST archive would move to the CfA. We summarize the contents of this collection regarding the instruments used and the spectra measured, and we present the tools and procedures we use for digitizing the collection. This includes the use of calibrated flatbed scanners for digitizing the plates themselves, as well as the digitization of correlated lab notebooks with important metadata associated with the plates.
tldr: The paper describes the transfer and digitization of the NIST Atomic Spectroscopy photographic glass plate archive into the Harvard Plate Stacks collection.
motivation: The closure of the NIST Atomic Spectroscopy Group in March 2025 left a large, irreplaceable collection of spectroscopic glass plate negatives without a home, requiring relocation to an institution with archival expertise.
method: The collection was moved to the Harvard Plate Stacks at the Center for Astrophysics, where calibrated flatbed scanners are used to digitize the plates, and correlated laboratory notebooks are digitized to capture associated metadata.
result: The authors summarize the contents of the collection—including the instruments used and spectra measured—and present the tools and procedures employed for digitization.
conclusion: The work preserves a historically significant spectroscopic archive and makes its data and metadata accessible through systematic digitization at Harvard.

title: Warp-Geo: Differentiable Geometry Representation For Dynamic-Boundary Simulation And Shape Optimization
authors: Weijie Zhang, Xiantao Fan, Jian-Xun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern inverse problems and adaptive simulations require efficient and differentiable representations of complex geometries that can be updated frequently for gradient-based optimization. Existing methods cannot simultaneously achieve both. We present Warp-Geo, a differentiable GPU-accelerated framework for reconstructing signed distance fields and evaluating surface normals from point clouds of complex 3D geometries. Warp-Geo combines uniform grids for GPU parallelism with implicit differentiation through the Poisson solve, enabling frequent geometry recomputation while maintaining full differentiability. We demonstrate Warp-Geo on forward SDF reconstruction, dynamic fluid--structure interaction with moving boundaries, and inverse shape optimization via automatic differentiation with gradient validation. GPU scalability analysis confirms practical feasibility for frequent geometry updates. The framework, implemented in Warp and JAX, enables seamless integration with differentiable physics solvers for end-to-end shape optimization.
tldr: Warp-Geo is a differentiable, GPU-accelerated framework that reconstructs signed distance fields and surface normals from point clouds to support dynamic-boundary simulation and gradient-based shape optimization.
motivation: Inverse problems and adaptive simulations need geometry representations that are both frequently updatable and fully differentiable for gradient-based optimization, a combination existing methods fail to provide.
method: The framework combines uniform grids for GPU parallelism with implicit differentiation through a Poisson solve, enabling frequent, differentiable recomputation of SDFs from point clouds.
result: The authors demonstrate forward SDF reconstruction, dynamic fluid–structure interaction with moving boundaries, and inverse shape optimization via automatic differentiation, with gradient validation and GPU scalability analysis.
conclusion: Warp-Geo, implemented in Warp and JAX, integrates seamlessly with differentiable physics solvers for end-to-end shape optimization.

title: Square Root Gauss-Newton iLQR
authors: Jur van Den Berg Maximilian Haas-Heger
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR) is a widely used algorithm for nonlinear trajectory optimization. At each iteration, it solves a local linear-quadratic approximation of the problem via dynamic programming, propagating a quadratic cost-to-go function. If the Hessian of the cost-to-go approximation is positive-semidefinite, one can derive a square root formulation of iLQR that propagates its Cholesky factor instead. This offers significant numerical advantages - much as square root Kalman filters improve upon their conventional counterparts - particularly when iLQR is used within an augmented Lagrangian framework for handling constraints, where large penalties degrade conditioning. Previous square root formulations of iLQR and related algorithms exist, but they are either numerically suboptimal, algorithmically complex, or both. In this paper, we show that the key to an effective square root formulation lies in the Gauss-Newton (weighted least-squares) structure of the cost function: this yields a positive semidefiniteness property that extends beyond the Hessian to the full augmented cost-to-go matrix, and enables a backward pass of remarkable simplicity in which each step reduces to a single QR-decomposition, from which the feedback gain and propagated Cholesky factor are extracted directly.
tldr: The paper introduces a square root formulation of iLQR that exploits the Gauss-Newton (weighted least-squares) structure of the cost to propagate Cholesky factors via a single QR decomposition per backward step.
motivation: Iterative LQR suffers from numerical ill-conditioning, especially within augmented Lagrangian frameworks where large penalties degrade the conditioning of the quadratic cost-to-go approximation; existing square root formulations are numerically suboptimal or algorithmically complex.
method: The authors show that the Gauss-Newton structure of the cost function implies positive semidefiniteness of the full augmented cost-to-go matrix, not just its Hessian, enabling a simplified backward pass in which each step reduces to one QR decomposition that directly yields the feedback gain and propagated Cholesky factor.
result: The proposed square root iLQR is derived with a remarkably simple backward recursion, improving numerical robustness and conditioning relative to previous square root and conventional iLQR implementations.
conclusion: Exploiting the weighted least-squares structure of the cost is the key to an effective, numerically stable square root iLQR suitable for constrained trajectory optimization.

title: Delay Equations With Measure-valued Coefficients: From Carath\'eodory Solutions To Measurable Semiflows
authors: Marek Kryspin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linear delay differential equations whose delay terms are represented by time-dependent finite signed measures. This framework accommodates discrete, distributed, and singular delay contributions without requiring continuity of the coefficient paths in time. We establish well-posedness in the Carath\'eodory sense and sequential dependence of solutions on the measure-valued parameters under almost-everywhere weak-* convergence and a common total variation bound. A central part of the analysis associates a signed measure on the time--delay domain with each coefficient path and establishes an equivalent integral formulation. This representation yields three equivalent characterizations of a [MATH]-algebra on the parameter space suited to measurability of the continuation operator. A measurable fixed-point argument then provides measurability of the solution maps, despite the possible failure of continuity in the product weak-* topology. For coefficients generated by a measure-preserving base flow, these results lead to measurable linear skew-product semiflows on continuous and absolutely continuous phase spaces. Under additional ergodic hypotheses and the assumption of a finite top Lyapunov exponent, eventual compactness and regularization yield Oseledets decompositions with the same Lyapunov exponents and multiplicities on both spaces.
tldr: The paper develops well-posedness theory and measurable semiflow/Oseledets decomposition results for linear delay differential equations whose delay terms are given by time-dependent finite signed measures.
motivation: Delay differential equations with measure-valued coefficients generalize discrete, distributed, and singular delays, but existing well-posedness and ergodic theory typically assumes continuity of coefficient paths in time, which is restrictive.
method: The authors establish Carathéodory well-posedness and continuous dependence under almost-everywhere weak-* convergence with a common total variation bound, associating a signed measure on the time-delay domain to each coefficient path to obtain an equivalent integral formulation and three characterizations of a suitable measurable algebra on the parameter space.
result: A measurable fixed-point argument yields measurability of solution maps, giving measurable linear skew-product semiflows on continuous and absolutely continuous phase spaces, and under ergodic hypotheses and finite top Lyapunov exponent, Oseledets decompositions with identical Lyapunov exponents and multiplicities on both spaces.
conclusion: The framework unifies discrete, distributed, and singular delay contributions without temporal continuity assumptions, extending multiplicative ergodic theory for such equations.

title: Mathematics Graduate Training In The Age Of Ai
authors: David Glickenstein
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI changes the conditions under which graduate mathematics is learned, assessed, written, and defended. The central claim of this paper is that mathematics graduate programs should respond to the moment by clarifying what graduate mathematics education is trying to teach and assess. In most ways, the goals of mathematics education have not changed. Rather, with changing tools it has become more essential than ever to make clear the goals of mathematical training. We use the term mathematical judgment to refer to the capacity to evaluate mathematics (e.g., claims, definitions, examples, proofs, analogies, computations, uses of tools, research directions) as mathematically sound, useful, well-posed, and appropriately justified. The recommendation is to center training on mathematical judgment, and we examine possible policies for graduate programs in Mathematics to this end.
tldr: The paper argues that mathematics graduate programs should restructure their training and assessment around cultivating 'mathematical judgment' in response to generative AI tools.
motivation: Generative AI is changing how graduate mathematics is learned, written, assessed, and defended, prompting a need to clarify the goals of mathematical education.
method: A conceptual/policy discussion that defines mathematical judgment as the capacity to evaluate claims, definitions, examples, proofs, analogies, computations, tool use, and research directions, then examines possible graduate-program policies.
result: The goals of mathematics education are largely unchanged, but clarifying them has become more urgent; centering training on mathematical judgment is proposed as the organizing principle.
conclusion: Mathematics graduate programs should explicitly define and assess mathematical judgment, and the paper sketches policy options for doing so.

title: Energy Stability And Error Estimates For A Second-order Structure-preserving Exponential Integrator Method For smectic-A Liquid Crystals
authors: Wenshuai Hu, Guanghua Ji, Xiao Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a second-order, linear, decoupled, and structure-preserving numerical scheme for the modified Landau--de Gennes model of smectic-A (SmA) liquid crystals. The main contributions are threefold. First, to the best of our knowledge, we propose the first integration of the generalized scalar auxiliary variable (GSAV) approach with a second-order exponential time-differencing Runge--Kutta (ETDRK2) discretization, leading to a second-order GSAV--ETD2 scheme. Second, we prove that the proposed scheme satisfies an unconditional energy-dissipation law, thereby closing the theoretical gap in the energy-stability analysis of second-order GSAV exponential integrators of this class. Third, by deriving a coercive discrete reformulation, we establish a fully discrete error estimate without imposing any coupling condition between [MATH] and [MATH], achieving the optimal convergence rate [MATH]. Numerical experiments are presented to verify our theoretical results and to simulate the self-assembly dynamics of the SmA phase.
tldr: The paper develops a second-order, linear, decoupled, structure-preserving exponential integrator scheme for the modified Landau–de Gennes model of smectic-A liquid crystals, with unconditional energy dissipation and optimal error estimates.
motivation: Numerical simulation of smectic-A liquid crystal dynamics requires schemes that are stable, accurate, and respect the underlying energy-dissipation structure without restrictive coupling conditions on the mesh and time step.
method: The authors combine the generalized scalar auxiliary variable (GSAV) approach with a second-order exponential time-differencing Runge–Kutta (ETDRK2) discretization, and derive a coercive discrete reformulation to obtain a fully discrete error estimate.
result: The scheme is proven to satisfy an unconditional energy-dissipation law, and an optimal convergence rate is established without any coupling condition between spatial and temporal discretization parameters; numerical experiments confirm the theory and reproduce SmA self-assembly dynamics.
conclusion: The work closes a theoretical gap in the energy-stability analysis of second-order GSAV exponential integrators and provides a robust tool for simulating smectic-A liquid crystal systems.

title: Complete Characterization Of Planar $c^1$ Linearizability And Optimal Conjugacy Regularity
authors: Yong Li Zhicheng Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a complete characterization of local [MATH] linearizability for planar diffeomorphisms. For every prescribed hyperbolic real Jordan form, we obtain necessary and sufficient integrability conditions on the modulus of continuity of the derivative for local [MATH] linearizability. These criteria reduce to three canonical thresholds: the classical, polynomially weighted, and squared-logarithmically weighted Dini conditions. Each threshold is optimal: whenever the corresponding condition fails, we construct a diffeomorphism with the identical linear part that is not locally [MATH] linearizable. For every non-hyperbolic linear part, explicit polynomial counterexamples show that smoothness alone cannot guarantee even local topological linearization. Beyond [MATH] existence, we determine the optimal regularity for the derivative of the linearizing conjugacy in every hyperbolic case, with the optimality established by counterexamples.
tldr: The paper gives a complete characterization of local C^1 linearizability for planar diffeomorphisms in terms of Dini-type conditions on the derivative's modulus of continuity, along with optimal conjugacy regularity.
motivation: Local linearization (conjugacy to a linear normal form) is a classical problem in dynamical systems, but the sharp conditions on derivative regularity that guarantee it were not fully determined.
method: The authors derive necessary and sufficient integrability conditions on the modulus of continuity of the derivative for each hyperbolic real Jordan form, and construct explicit counterexamples (including polynomial ones for non-hyperbolic parts) to prove optimality.
result: Local C^1 linearizability is characterized by exactly three canonical thresholds — the classical, polynomially weighted, and squared-logarithmically weighted Dini conditions — and the optimal regularity of the linearizing conjugacy's derivative is determined in every hyperbolic case.
conclusion: The work completely settles the smooth linearizability problem at the C^1 level for planar diffeomorphisms, showing smoothness alone is insufficient in non-hyperbolic cases.

title: Dimension-free Weak $(1,1)$ Estimates For Riesz Transforms With Constant Drift
authors: Suman Mukherjee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] on [MATH], where [MATH] is a constant drift vector. We prove that the full vector Riesz transform [MATH] satisfies a weak-type [MATH] estimate for real-valued functions with constant at most [MATH], uniformly in both the dimension and the drift vector. Our proof extends the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector and Stockdale ([URL] to the exponentially weighted setting. Interpolation then yields strong [MATH] bounds for [MATH], with constants depending only on [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves dimension-free weak (1,1) bounds for Riesz transforms associated with a constant-drift diffusion operator, extending a fractional obstacle method to the exponentially weighted setting.
motivation: Riesz transform estimates for drifted operators are of interest in harmonic analysis, where dimension-free bounds quantify how constants behave uniformly across dimension and drift.
method: The authors extend the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale to an exponentially weighted (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-like) setting to establish weak-type (1,1) estimates.
result: The full vector Riesz transform satisfies a weak-type (1,1) estimate with a constant independent of both the dimension and the drift vector, and interpolation yields corresponding strong L^p bounds.
conclusion: The work provides sharp dimension-free and drift-independent Riesz transform bounds, contributing to classical harmonic analysis of drifted diffusions.

title: A Formalisation Of A Special Case Of The Union-Closed Conjecture In Isabelle/HOL
authors: Lawrence C. Paulson Angeliki Koutsoukou-Argyraki
abstract: ArXiv:2609.20876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A 2021 proof of a special case of the Union-Closed Conjecture, by Aaronson, Ellis and Leader, has been formalised in the proof assistant Isabelle/HOL. Our discussion involves sketching their proof and displaying snippets from the Isabelle version of the proof, illustrating the extent to which mathematical reasoning can be rendered clearly in a formal language.
tldr: The authors formalize a special case of the Union-Closed Conjecture, due to Aaronson, Ellis and Leader, in the Isabelle/HOL proof assistant.
motivation: The Union-Closed Conjecture is a long-standing open problem in combinatorics, and formal verification offers a way to guarantee the correctness of partial progress while exploring how mathematical reasoning can be expressed in a formal language.
method: The 2021 proof of a special case is reconstructed in Isabelle/HOL, with the paper sketching the mathematical argument and displaying representative Isabelle proof snippets.
result: A complete machine-checked formalization of the special case is achieved, alongside a discussion of how clearly the underlying mathematical reasoning can be rendered in formal syntax.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the feasibility of formalizing contemporary combinatorial research in Isabelle/HOL, though it has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Sources Of Unknowability And Self-refutation In Epistemic And Dynamic Epistemic Logic
authors: Eiji Yamada
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we define a formula [MATH] to be unbelievable if [MATH] is unsatisfiable, and unknowable if [MATH] is unsatisfiable. We then analyze the sources of unknowability and unbelievability in different classes of frames K, KD, KD45, and S5. We first show that any unbelievable formula is a fixed point of the Moore function defined by [MATH] Our main result shows that in S5, the static notions of unknowability and unbelievability in epistemic logic, and the dynamic notions of always informativeness and eventual self-refutation in dynamic epistemic logic are all equivalent to ``Moorean phenomena.'' We also generalize the result to the multi-agent case, showing that although all unknowable formulas still manifest Moorean phenomena, new mechanisms arise due to their interactive nature. Finally, we briefly analyze whether the Brandenburger-Keisler paradox in epistemic game theory can be considered Moorean.
tldr: The paper analyzes unknowability and unbelievability in epistemic and dynamic epistemic logic, showing they coincide with Moorean phenomena in S5 and generalizing to multi-agent settings.
motivation: To identify the logical sources of unknowability, unbelievability, and self-refutation across different modal frame classes.
method: The authors define unknowable and unbelievable formulas, prove fixed-point properties of the Moore function, and compare static and dynamic epistemic notions in K, KD, KD45, and S5 frames.
result: In S5, unknowability, unbelievability, always informativeness, and eventual self-refutation are all equivalent to Moorean phenomena; multi-agent cases introduce new interactive mechanisms.
conclusion: Moorean phenomena underlie various epistemic and dynamic epistemic paradoxes, though multi-agent interaction yields additional mechanisms; the Brandenburger-Keisler paradox is briefly examined.

title: A Framework To Quantify The Probability Of Future Cyber Loss Events
authors: Martin Eian Siem Peters
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cybersecurity risk quantification remains challenging due to limited operational data and difficulties in quantifying Loss Event Frequency (LEF). This paper introduces the Loss Event Frequency Security Analyser (LEFSA), a probabilistic framework that reformulates LEF estimation as machine-level Cyber Loss Event (CLE) prediction combined with hierarchical infrastructure-level aggregation. LEFSA estimates calibrated machine-level CLE probabilities from operational cybersecurity telemetry and aggregates them across infrastructure layers while accounting for machine-level dependencies. This provides a foundation for scalable, explainable, and operationally applicable cyber risk estimation at the level of machines, services, business processes, and the entire organization. The framework was evaluated using proprietary Managed Detection & Response telemetry from 23 organizations using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. XGBoost achieved the strongest predictive performance, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 and consistently low calibration error across evaluation periods. The results demonstrate that operational cybersecurity telemetry contains substantial predictive information for future CLE occurrence, supporting probabilistic machine-level modeling and hierarchical aggregation as a promising foundation for quantitative, data-driven cyber risk management.
tldr: LEFSA is a probabilistic framework that predicts machine-level Cyber Loss Event probabilities from operational telemetry and hierarchically aggregates them into organization-level cyber risk estimates.
motivation: Cybersecurity risk quantification is difficult because loss event frequency (LEF) is hard to estimate with limited operational data and existing methods lack scalability and explainability.
method: The framework trains calibrated machine-level CLE classifiers (XGBoost performing best) on Managed Detection & Response telemetry from 23 organizations using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, then aggregates predictions across infrastructure layers while modeling machine-level dependencies.
result: XGBoost achieved a mean AUC of 0.90 with consistently low calibration error across evaluation periods, showing operational security telemetry carries substantial predictive signal for future loss events.
conclusion: Probabilistic machine-level modeling plus hierarchical aggregation offers a scalable, explainable foundation for data-driven cyber risk management, though the work is entirely classical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, or networks.

title: On The Reconstruction Of Sas From Other Triangle Congruence Criteria, Part Ii: Eliminating The Pons Asinorum
authors: Roberto Volpe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the first part of this work we showed that, within a Hilbert plane deprived of the Side-Angle-Side axiom, the Side-Angle-Angle criterion, together with a ray correspondence principle [], the existence of angle bisectors [], the congruence of supplements of congruent angles [], and the Pons Asinorum [], suffices to reconstruct SAS. We left open the question of whether [] is genuinely required alongside the other three principles, noting only a qualitative asymmetry in the nature of the principles involved. In this second part we answer this question: we show that ,\ [],\ [] \;\vdash\; [], so that [] is redundant among the hypotheses of our main theorem, which improves to ,\ [],\ [],\ [] \;\vdash\; . The proof adapts an argument recently given by Donnelly, who reconstructs SAS from SAA together with an angle addition axiom and the existence of angle bisectors.
tldr: The paper proves that in a Hilbert plane without the Side-Angle-Side axiom, the Side-Angle-Angle criterion plus angle bisectors, supplement congruence, and the Pons Asinorum suffice to reconstruct SAS, rendering an earlier ray correspondence principle redundant.
motivation: This work addresses a foundational question in axiomatic Euclidean geometry: whether a previously assumed ray correspondence principle is genuinely necessary for reconstructing the SAS congruence criterion.
method: The proof adapts a recent argument by Donnelly, which reconstructs SAS from SAA together with an angle addition axiom and the existence of angle bisectors, and shows that the ray correspondence principle is derivable from the other axioms.
result: The main result eliminates the ray correspondence principle from the hypothesis set, improving the axiom system to SAA, angle bisectors, supplement congruence, and Pons Asinorum ⊢ SAS.
conclusion: The Pons Asinorum is redundant among the hypotheses, and the reconstruction of SAS in a Hilbert plane without the SAS axiom is established under a weaker set of assumptions.

title: Loopjacking: Hijacking Human-in-the-Loop Approval
authors: Adithyan Arun Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human approval is often treated as the last security boundary before an agent executes a consequential operation. That boundary is only meaningful if the operation presented for review is the operation later authorized or released. We call failures of this binding Loopjacking: a human approves what they understand as operation A, while the implementation uses that decision for a materially different operation B. We distinguish two variants. In a representation-based attack, B is already encoded but omitted or misrepresented at approval time; in a post-approval state-substitution attack, the human sees the correct A and mutable workflow state later replaces it with B. We evaluate a purposive set of released agent products. We reproduce post-approval substitution in seven tested Agno AgentOS releases ending at 3.0.9 and in 12 tested versions of a conditional in-memory LangGraph Agent Server composition ending at 0.14.0. We reproduce representation mismatch in OpenClaw 2026.2.23 and its rejection in 2026.2.24. OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0 and 0.22.2 provide a negative control: serialized continuation preserves exact per-call binding and rejects mutated B. These results do not estimate ecosystem prevalence. They show that complete canonical approval rendering and exact use-time comparison, or preventing unauthorized pending-state mutation, block the tested attacks while preserving legitimate execution. We separate this contribution from established work on misleading dialogs, session smuggling, action binding, and authorization continuity.
tldr: The paper defines and demonstrates 'Loopjacking,' an attack where human approval for one operation is bound to a different operation executed by an AI agent framework.
motivation: Human approval is often treated as a security boundary for AI agents, but this boundary fails if the approved operation and the executed operation differ.
method: The authors test released agent products, including Agno AgentOS, LangGraph Agent Server, OpenClaw, and OpenAI Agents SDK, for representation-based and post-approval state-substitution attacks.
result: Post-approval substitution was reproduced in seven Agno AgentOS releases and 12 LangGraph versions; representation mismatch was reproduced in OpenClaw 2026.2.23 but rejected in 2026.2.24, while OpenAI Agents SDK versions served as a negative control.
conclusion: Complete canonical approval rendering and exact use-time comparison, or preventing unauthorized pending-state mutation, can block the tested attacks while preserving legitimate execution.

title: Toss If Perishable: An Ethnographic Study On Building Scenario-Based Training For Non-Perishable Skills
authors: Francis Hahn, Spencer Cherry, Kumar Shashwat, Laura Araujo Buldrini, Daniel Lende, Xinming Ou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security Operations Centers (SOCs) often rely upon on-the-job training focusing on the specific tools and procedures a SOC utilizes. The complexity in tooling can overshadow the underlying reasoning process, hindering an analyst's ability to learn investigative skills. We formulate the concept of "non-perishable knowledge" which corresponds to investigative thinking skills independent of tools. We developed a scenario-driven training method to understand whether such non-perishable knowledge can be imparted through specially designed incident scenarios, where trainees are presented with and solve investigative challenges in a tool-agnostic manner. We designed two such scenarios based on real-world incidents. Human subjects were recruited from a university's student body for ethnographic study to understand how this training method is received by the subjects and how they perform on such tasks. We collected data from 20 hours of documented training with 25 trainees spread across five sessions. Using grounded-theory, we analyzed the data and uncovered factors that inhibit or promote learning of the investigative thinking skills. Our research combines scenario-based training, ethnographic research, and technical analysis to examine how to best train students in the reasoning skills that industry deems vital to SOCs.
tldr: An ethnographic study of scenario-based, tool-agnostic training designed to teach 'non-perishable' investigative reasoning skills to Security Operations Center analysts.
motivation: SOC training tends to focus on specific tools and procedures, which can obscure the underlying investigative reasoning that industry considers essential, so the authors ask whether such tool-independent thinking can be taught deliberately.
method: Two incident scenarios based on real-world events were designed and delivered to 25 trainees across five sessions (20 hours of documented training); data were collected ethnographically and analyzed using grounded theory to identify factors promoting or inhibiting learning.
result: The analysis uncovered specific factors that inhibit or promote the acquisition of investigative thinking skills, and demonstrated that scenario-driven, tool-agnostic training is received in ways that shape skill development.
conclusion: Scenario-based training combined with ethnographic methods can be used to design more effective education in the non-perishable reasoning skills valued by SOCs.

title: Identifying Security Platform Product Abuse With Machine Learning
authors: Shaefer Drew, Michael Brautbar, Paul Knight, Edward Raff, Lana Peric-Mcdermott, Simran Sarin, Nickolas Machado, Hanna Albright, Vitaly Zaytsev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Product abuse is an individually rare, but growing, problem across the SaaS industry. Highly sophisticated threat actors can misuse security platforms within customer environments or conduct bypass experiments on the product itself. Threat actors can leverage living-off-the-land (LOTL) attacks to avoid using cumbersome, frequently detected malware. Remediating this threat requires collecting multiple data modalities across different types of databases, addressing a cold-start problem in the intrinsic rarity of such sophisticated but dangerous events, and designing within the constraints of real-world deployment (e.g., cost, user behavior, performance, etc). To wit, we provide the first study of such a whole-system defense, especially with respect to a deployed and operational capability. Our results show an increase in product abuse coverage by 35\%, a 30\% reduction in monthly alerts, and adaptability to changes in malicious actors' behavior. We review both the constraints we considered in designing the system to meet operational requirements and a retrospective evaluation of the value of explainable features and counterfactual performance on previously identified attacks.
tldr: This paper presents a machine learning system for detecting product abuse in security platforms, addressing a rare but growing threat in SaaS environments.
motivation: Product abuse by sophisticated threat actors is individually rare but increasing across the SaaS industry, requiring defenses that handle multiple data modalities and cold-start rarity while meeting real-world deployment constraints.
method: The authors design a whole-system defense that collects multiple data modalities from different databases, addresses the cold-start problem, and operates within cost, user behavior, and performance constraints using machine learning.
result: The deployed system increases product abuse coverage by 35%, reduces monthly alerts by 30%, and adapts to changes in malicious actors' behavior, with retrospective evaluation of explainable features and counterfactual performance.
conclusion: This is the first study of a whole-system defense for security platform product abuse, demonstrating operational value through improved coverage, reduced alert volume, and adaptability.

title: Et Tu, MacBook? Unprivileged Keystroke Inference And Context Profiling Via The Built-in Imu Side Channel
authors: Jiaji He, Yi Shi, Junfeng Cai, Chang Liu, Yongqiang Lyu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent generations of Apple MacBooks embed an inertial measurement unit (IMU) within their unibody chassis for device orientation and motion sensing. However, this IMU inadvertently captures not only intended device-level information but also subtle physical vibrations from user interactions and the surrounding environment. These signals establish a novel, previously unexplored side channel. We uncover a vulnerability allowing non-root access to IMU data via an IOKit driver, alongside two content-free system metadata interfaces (HIDIdleTime and CGEventSource) that further enrich the side-channel leakage. Through rigorous characterization of the IMU data, we reveal that the leakage spans three core dimensions: (1) keystroke identity (which key is typed), (2) desk surface (where the laptop is placed), and (3) user behavior (who is typing). Leveraging these findings, we introduce BRUTUS, the first comprehensive unprivileged side-channel attack targeting built-in IMU sensors on Apple MacBooks. BRUTUS achieves a character-level accuracy of 89.1% to 97.5% in key recovery. Furthermore, aided by language models, it can successfully reconstruct certain sentences with 100% accuracy. For user identification and environment profiling, BRUTUS correctly discovers user and environment profiles without labels and correctly assigns subsequent segments to their corresponding profiles. Ultimately, this work highlights the urgent necessity of strictly regulating access to built-in IMU sensors.
tldr: BRUTUS is an unprivileged side-channel attack that uses MacBook built-in IMU data to infer keystrokes, desk surface, and user identity.
motivation: Built-in IMUs on Apple MacBooks are accessible without root and inadvertently capture physical vibrations from typing and the environment, creating a novel privacy and security side channel.
method: The authors characterize IMU signals accessible via an IOKit driver plus HIDIdleTime and CGEventSource metadata, then build BRUTUS to classify keystroke identity, desk surface, and user behavior, using language models for sentence reconstruction.
result: BRUTUS achieves 89.1–97.5% character-level key recovery, 100% sentence reconstruction in some cases, and label-free profiling of users and environments.
conclusion: The work exposes an urgent need to restrict unprivileged access to built-in IMU sensors on laptops.

title: TERMon: Detecting Persistent Behavioral Threats In Edge Ai Via Hardware-Native Ternary Runtime Monitor
authors: Edlira Dushku Arish Sateesan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Edge AI accelerators are increasingly deployed in safety-critical environments, where model outputs may control physical actuators, make access-control decisions, or trigger alarms. In these settings, runtime failures often remain undetected because model corruption, distribution shift, and adversarial inputs can still produce well-formed, confident predictions. This paper presents TERMon, a lightweight hardware runtime monitor that detects such anomalies by observing inference behavior rather than re-executing or formally verifying the model. TERMon represents class-conditional trusted behavior as hardware-efficient ternary patterns that are matched in parallel against a thermometer-encoded fingerprint. The ternary encoding reproduces the corresponding unquantized range decision exactly. TERMon detects harmful weight corruptions in proportion to their behavioral impact, while out-of-distribution and adversarial inputs are largely not separable using the monitored features at a strict false-positive operating point. We implemented TERMon on a PYNQ-Z2 FPGA, and the pipelined design requires no on-chip block RAM or DSPs and has a two-cycle decision latency.
tldr: TERMon is a hardware-based runtime monitor for edge AI that detects weight corruption via ternary pattern matching on FPGA but fails to separate out-of-distribution and adversarial inputs.
motivation: Edge AI accelerators used in safety-critical tasks can fail silently because corrupted models, distribution shifts, and adversarial examples still yield confident predictions.
method: The monitor encodes class-conditional trusted behavior as hardware-efficient ternary patterns matched in parallel against a thermometer-encoded inference fingerprint on a PYNQ-Z2 FPGA.
result: TERMon detects harmful weight corruptions proportionally to their behavioral impact, while OOD and adversarial inputs remain largely undetectable at a strict false-positive operating point, with no BRAM or DSP usage and two-cycle latency.
conclusion: Hardware-native behavioral monitoring enables low-overhead corruption detection for edge AI, but broader anomaly detection remains limited, and the work is unrelated to quantum information research.

title: Interference-Driven Clustered Optimisation For Fm Spectrum Coordination
authors: Emiliano Pallotti Federica Mangiatordi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-border FM spectrum coordination involves protecting foreign broadcasting services while preserving domestic coverage, amid increasingly large radio-planning datasets containing thousands of transmitters and millions of transmitter-pixel relationships. In such scenarios, conventional optimisation approaches become computationally demanding due to the high dimensionality of the associated power-control problem. This paper proposes an interference-driven clustered optimisation framework for large-scale FM spectrum coordination. The proposed method exploits the observation that violations of foreign-service protection are typically dominated by a limited subset of transmitters. Protected services are therefore analysed to identify dominant interferers and quantify their impact on interference. These relationships are represented through an interference graph from which optimisation-oriented transmitter clusters are extracted. The clusters decompose the global power-control problem into smaller optimisation tasks solved with clustered simulated annealing, followed by a global refinement that captures residual inter-cluster interactions. Coverage and interference are evaluated using frequency-dependent protection criteria and a dynamic strongest-service assignment model. To enable operational-scale planning, the framework uses sparse matrices and GPU-accelerated computations. Tests on realistic cross-border FM coordination scenarios show that the clustering strategy greatly reduces optimisation complexity and runtime while maintaining foreign-service protection and domestic coverage. The method also yields an interpretable ranking of transmitters that contribute most to harmful interference, supporting optimisation and spectrum planning.
tldr: A clustering-based optimization framework using interference graphs and GPU-accelerated simulated annealing for large-scale cross-border FM spectrum coordination.
motivation: Cross-border FM spectrum coordination involves thousands of transmitters and millions of transmitter-pixel relationships, making conventional power-control optimization computationally prohibitive.
method: The authors identify dominant interferers via an interference graph, extract optimization-oriented transmitter clusters, solve subproblems with clustered simulated annealing, and apply a global refinement step, using sparse matrices and GPU acceleration.
result: Tests on realistic cross-border scenarios show greatly reduced optimization complexity and runtime while preserving foreign-service protection and domestic coverage, plus an interpretable ranking of harmful interferers.
conclusion: The framework offers a scalable and interpretable tool for operational-scale FM spectrum planning, though it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Combining Exploratory Analysis And Automated Analysis For Anomaly Detection In Real-Time Data Streams
authors: Ahmed Shah, Ibrahim Abualhaol, Mahmoud Gad, Michael Weiss
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security analysts can become overwhelmed with monitoring real-time security information that is important to help them defend their network. They also tend to focus on a limited portion of the alerts, and therefore risk missing important events and links between them. At the heart of the problem is the system that analysts use to detect, explore, and respond to cyber-attacks. Developers of security analysis systems face the challenge of developing a system that can present different sources of information at multiple levels of abstraction, while also creating a system that is intuitive to use. In this article, we examine the complementary nature of exploratory analysis and automated analysis by testing the development of a system that monitors real-time Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) traffic for anomalies that might indicate security threats. BGP is an essential component for supporting the infrastructure of the Internet; however, it is also highly vulnerable and can be hijacked by attackers to propagate spam or launch denial-of-service attacks. Some of the attack scenarios on the BGP infrastructure can be quite elaborate, and it is difficult, if not impossible, to fully automate the detection of such attacks. This article makes two contributions: i) it describes a prototype platform for computing indicators and threat alerts in real time and for visualizing the context of an alert, and ii) it discusses the interaction of exploratory analysis (visualization) and automated analysis. This article is relevant to students, security researchers, and developers who are interested in the development or use of real-time security monitoring systems. They will gain insights into the complementary aspects of automated analysis and exploratory analysis through the development of a real-time streaming system.
tldr: This paper presents a prototype system for real-time BGP anomaly detection that combines automated threat alerts with exploratory visual analysis for security analysts.
motivation: Security analysts monitoring real-time network traffic are overwhelmed by alerts and may miss important threats, especially in BGP infrastructure that is highly vulnerable to hijacking and denial-of-service attacks.
method: The authors develop a streaming platform that computes indicators and threat alerts in real time from BGP traffic, and they study the complementary interaction between automated analysis and exploratory visualization.
result: The prototype demonstrates that combining automated detection with exploratory analysis can help analysts perceive context and identify elaborate BGP attack scenarios that are difficult to fully automate.
conclusion: The work provides insights for developers of real-time security monitoring systems, highlighting the value of integrating automated and exploratory approaches, though it is unrelated to quantum information research.

title: Astra: Toward Agentic Ai For Intelligent Device-Network-Cloud Synergy In Next-Generation Mobile Communication
authors: Yalong Guo, Jinbo Tan, Ying Wang, Fan Zhang, Jintao Wang, Changyong Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The evolution toward next-generation mobile communication systems demands intelligence-native networks capable of autonomously adapting to user intent, yet the prevailing 3GPP protocol-driven device-network-cloud (DNC) architecture imposes three structural bottlenecks: protocol-constrained decision spaces confining optimization to predefined parameter subsets, cascaded information asymmetry from lossy interface compression that strips semantic context and causes intent miscalibration, and inherently reactive coordination mechanisms that trigger actions only after performance degradation. This paper proposes an autonomous agentic AI paradigm named Agentic Synergy for Telecommunication Resource Autonomy (ASTRA), which introduces a three-tier agent layer, including device agent, network agent, and cloud agent, decoupling network intelligence from the underlying hardware infrastructure. These agents collaborate through bidirectional semantic channels, including semantic intent messages, capability abstraction messages, global directives, and peer coordination, executing a six-phase cycle of perceive, reason and predict, communicate, decide, act, and learn that transforms reactive protocol-driven operations into proactive, intent-calibrated optimization over the full decision space. Validated through system-level simulations in two representative scenarios, ASTRA achieves a 13.1\% average throughput gain in dense-crowd cell selection by redistributing UEs from congested cells via semantic load exchange, and an 18.2\% passive handover reduction in high-speed mobility through predictive trajectory-aware coordination, providing initial evidence that the proposed agentic framework accesses solution regions structurally inaccessible under protocol-constrained architectures.
tldr: ASTRA proposes a three-tier agentic AI framework for autonomous device-network-cloud coordination in next-generation mobile communication systems.
motivation: Next-generation mobile networks require intelligence-native, intent-driven adaptation, but current 3GPP protocol-driven architectures suffer from constrained decision spaces, information asymmetry, and reactive coordination.
method: The paper introduces a three-tier agent layer (device, network, cloud) that collaborates via bidirectional semantic channels and executes a six-phase perceive-reason-communicate-decide-act-learn cycle to enable proactive, intent-calibrated optimization.
result: System-level simulations show a 13.1% average throughput gain in dense-crowd cell selection and an 18.2% reduction in passive handovers in high-speed mobility scenarios.
conclusion: Agentic AI can access solution regions structurally inaccessible to protocol-constrained architectures, offering a promising paradigm for next-generation mobile communication systems.

title: Ultimate Information Rate For Quantum Sensing Under Multilevel Relaxation
authors: Changhun Oh, Seok Hyung Lie, Youngrong Lim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the ultimate information rate of a relaxing multilevel quantum sensor under unrestricted adaptive control and construct an explicit strategy that attains it. We consider sensing a weak field that couples the ground state to several excited states that decay back to the ground state, a setting that reduces to amplitude-damping sensing for a single excited state. We show that the ultimate information rate is exactly the mean population lifetime of the bright state coupled to the ground state by the signal. Although the sensing dynamics generally involve several decay modes, an explicit rank-one protocol that monitors the ground--bright coherence using fresh meters and classical feedback attains this rate while keeping its finite-time information deficit bounded by a constant. For independently relaxing identical sensors, independent local monitoring attains the sum of their individual optimal rates, so intersensor entanglement and joint quantum error correction cannot increase the asymptotic rate. Consequently, the free population-decay curve provides an operational measure of the optimal sensing performance under arbitrary adaptive control.

title: Quantum Loads And The Generalized Telegrapher's Problem
authors: A. Delattre E. Collin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on the mapping of classical microwave transmission line theory onto the quantum scattering matrix description. By means of a generalized flux formalism a la Devoret, we derive a charge-current vector living on the confining electrodes, to which a Hodge-like decomposition is applied. The presented theory holds equally well for all types of waves traveling within Cartesian and cylindrical guide geometries (the usual Transverse Electric Magnetic, but also Transverse Magnetic and Transverse Electric ones). We then demonstrate how a generic load decomposes into a series of complex coefficients [MATH], for each mode [MATH] propagating along the line. This decomposition leads to a particular classification of traveling waves: gradient-type and curl-type charge-currents. This distinction shines a new light on a broken gauge symmetry exhibited by a class of Transverse Electric modes. Our results provide a universal theoretical framework, which finds a direct usage in microwave-based quantum information transfer.

title: Optimal Control For Duty-cycle-limited Interferometry With single-NV Centers
authors: Ugur Tamer, Sina Zeytinoglu, Ozgur E. Mustecaplioglu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stimulus-responsive hydrogels convert temperature changes into magnetic-field shifts detectable by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, enabling nanoscale thermometry in soft and biological environments. Existing hydrogel-nanodiamond demonstrations rely on NV ensembles, whose high photon throughput is accompanied by gradient-induced inhomogeneous broadening, while idealized single-NV projections assume high-fluence fluorescence/ODMR readout. Here we study a pulsed single-NV route for the same class of sensors and ask whether decoherence-aware coherent control can improve thermometric performance over optimized Ramsey interrogation at equal detected-photon budget. Using a sigmoidal volume-phase-transition model, dipolar magnetic transduction, and Lindblad master-equation simulations, we find a reproducible 25-27% per-shot sensitivity gain over optimized Ramsey, i.e., a 57-60% gain in Fisher information (1.57-1.60). The same gain carries over to the photon-normalized Fisher information. The rate gain is governed by the measurement duty cycle, the fraction of the experimental cycle spent accumulating signal rather than initializing, reading out or waiting, and becomes largest when the overhead or optical-dose constraint dominates the cycle time. The optimized trajectories reveal a response-shaping mechanism in which phase accumulation is concentrated near the end of the sequence, and a closed-form depth-two solution reproduces the numerical optimum and exhibits that mechanism analytically. The advantage is most pronounced when the dephasing time is short compared with the measurement overhead or dose-limited waiting time, which is the operating regime targeted by hydrogel-transduced single-spin biosensing.

title: Benign Nonconvex Landscape For Policy Optimization: Infinite-Horizon Discounted MDPs With General State And Action Spaces
authors: Minda Zhao Xin Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.21433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the optimization landscape for infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs) with general state and action spaces under structured stationary policy classes. A general weighted policy-iteration approach to establishing global convergence guarantees for policy gradient methods requires closure under weighted policy improvement at every policy, a property that may fail even when the policy class contains an optimal policy. To address this issue, we propose weaker conditions that guarantee the absence of suboptimal stationary points and establish the Polyak--Lojasiewicz--Kurdyka (PLK) condition for the policy gradient objective with a finite concentrability coefficient. We also establish the PLK condition from a policy-improvement bound that holds at every state, without a concentrability assumption. Our general results encompass settings covered by the earlier framework when the common standing assumptions hold for the same policy class and parameter domain. We further verify our proposed conditions for two operations models: inventory systems with Markov-modulated demand and stochastic cash-balance problems. For both models, the Bellman equation yields approximate convexity of the Q-value functions in the action variable, with deviations controlled by the first-order stationarity measure. These estimates establish exponent-one and, under additional curvature assumptions, exponent-two PLK conditions, which, together with Lipschitz continuity of the policy gradient, imply an [MATH] iteration complexity and linear convergence, respectively, for projected gradient descent using exact policy gradients. To the best of our knowledge, we provide the first non-asymptotic convergence rates for solving infinite-horizon discounted inventory systems with Markov-modulated demand and stochastic cash-balance problems using policy gradient methods.
tldr: This paper studies the optimization landscape of policy gradient methods for infinite-horizon discounted MDPs with general state and action spaces, establishing PLK conditions for global convergence under weaker assumptions.
motivation: Policy gradient methods lack global convergence guarantees in general MDPs because standard weighted policy iteration conditions can fail even when an optimal policy exists in the policy class.
method: The authors propose weaker conditions ensuring no suboptimal stationary points and establish the Polyak-Lojasiewicz-Kurdyka (PLK) condition with and without a concentrability assumption, then verify these conditions for inventory and stochastic cash-balance models.
result: They derive exponent-one and, under added curvature, exponent-two PLK conditions, yielding iteration complexity and linear convergence for projected gradient descent with exact policy gradients.
conclusion: The work provides the first non-asymptotic convergence rates for policy gradient methods on infinite-horizon discounted inventory systems with Markov-modulated demand and stochastic cash-balance problems.
